title: fix(web): strip ASCII control characters in getSafeRedirectPath
body:
## Bug: `getSafeRedirectPath` does not strip ASCII control characters, leaving new-line / RTL-override / null-byte paths through

### Problem

[`getSafeRedirectPath`](https://github.com/Harsh23Kashyap/langfuse/blob/2852b0cc6d83667e4ec22fa63331c71cde976ceb/web/src/utils/redirect.ts) trims whitespace and rejects protocol-relative / absolute / scheme-prefixed paths, but it does **not** strip ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F and 0x7F). Three known attack / foot-gun patterns exploit this gap:

1. **Newline injection.** A path like `/abc\nevil.com` passes the existing guards because `trimmed.startsWith("/")` is true and `trimmed.startsWith("//")` is false. Downstream URL parsers, log aggregators, and HTTP response headers can be confused by embedded `\n` (HTTP header injection / log forging) or by treating `\r` as a header terminator.
2. **Bidirectional text injection (RTL override).** `\u202e` (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) is a control character that flips the visual rendering of subsequent text. A path like `/abc\u202e\u202emojise\u202e.txt` could be used to disguise a malicious link. The current code only checks `startsWith("/")` and `startsWith("//")`; the control character stays in the path.
3. **Null-byte injection.** A path like `/dashboard\^@.png` could confuse path-extension or content-type detection downstream. `getSafeRedirectPath` passes the null byte through.

The existing test suite at [`web/src/__tests__/redirect.clienttest.ts`](https://github.com/Harsh23Kashyap/langfuse/blob/2852b0cc6d83667e4ec22fa63331c71cde976ceb/web/src/__tests__/redirect.clienttest.ts) (37 tests) does not cover new-line, control-character, or RTL-override injection. The only whitespace-related test is the `tab + trailing space` trim case on line 71, which uses `["  /dashboard  "]`, not embedded control characters.

### Current behavior

- `getSafeRedirectPath("/abc\nevil.com")` returns `"/abc\nevil.com"` (unsafe — passes the existing guards).
- `getSafeRedirectPath("/abc\u202eevil")` ret

title: bug: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ClickHouse migration incompatible with NFS filesystems (Amazon EFS)
body:
### Describe the bug

The ClickHouse migration introduced in  #14872 uses `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`, which is [incompatible with NFS-based filesystems](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/96835) such as Amazon EFS. When ClickHouse's data directory is backed by EFS, the `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` operation fails, causing the migration to fail. As a result, the ClickHouse server stops and does not come back up.

Expected behavior: migrations should complete successfully on NFS-based storage (e.g. Amazon EFS) and ClickHouse should remain running.

Proposed fix: replace CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW with DROP VIEW + CREATE VIEW to avoid the atomic-replace behavior that NFS does not support.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy self-hosted Langfuse with ClickHouse using an NFS-based filesystem (e.g. Amazon EFS) for the ClickHouse data directory.
2. Upgrade to a version including the changes from PR #14872 (https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/14872/files).
3. Run the ClickHouse migrations on startup.
4. The migration using CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fails, the migration aborts, and the ClickHouse server stops.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Self-hosted

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

The latest. We track the most recent v3 image on docker hub

_No response_

title: [Experiment Action] PR comment collision when a parallel matrix runs the same experiment script across legs
body:
# PR comment collision when a parallel matrix runs the same experiment script across legs

## Summary

When a workflow runs this action multiple times in one run as a **matrix that invokes the same
`experiment_path` with different parameters** (one leg per job, in parallel), the PR comment ends
up showing only **one** leg's results — the others are silently clobbered. The comment's
combine-into-sections feature can't distinguish legs that share a script, and the shared-comment
upsert races across parallel jobs.

Observed with `v1.0.5` (`377da5adb75223b208b7da05276598ff093aaf48`); the comment logic lives in
`src/comment.ts`.

## What happens

We run a discovery-driven matrix: one generic experiment script (`prompt-eval.experiment.ts`) is
invoked once per `(project, prompt)` leg, varying only env (`LANGFUSE_PROJECT`, `PROMPT_NAME`),
with `fail-fast: false` and default parallelism. Each leg is its own job. Expectation: each leg's
scores show up on the PR. Actual: exactly one comment per workflow run, containing only the
last-finishing leg (in our case OCR always overwrote Match).

## Reproduction

A workflow like:

```yaml
strategy:
  fail-fast: false
  matrix:
    include:
      - { prompt: A }
      - { prompt: B }
steps:
  - uses: langfuse/experiment-action@<sha>
    env:
      PROMPT_NAME: ${{ matrix.prompt }}
    with:
      experiment_path: scripts/one-generic-experiment.ts   # SAME path for every leg
      should_comment_on_pr: 'true'
      # ...
```

Two legs (A and B) run in parallel. Result: one PR comment showing only A or only B.

## Root cause

Two independent issues:

1. **Sections are keyed by script path only.** `sectionMarkers()` keys each experiment's section
   on `encodeURIComponent(scriptPath)`. The combine feature assumes "one experiment = one script
   file." When every leg runs the same `experiment_path`, all legs map to the **same** section
   and overwrite each other. There's no way to express `(script, parameters)` as distinct
   experiments.

title: bug(ui): Generations table Tokens per second column always empty (reads completionTokens, row has outputUsage)
body: ## Bug description In self-hosted **Langfuse OSS `v3.205.1`**, the **Tokens per second** column in the **Generations / Observations table** stays empty even when: - the column is enabled - the same generation has **Output Tokens > 0** - **Latency > 0** - **Time to first token** is present - **Dashboard** widgets correctly show tokens/s for the same data So this is not a missing-usage / missing-TTFT ingestion problem. Dashboard works; the Generations table column does not. ## Expected behavior Generations table **Tokens per second** should render something like: `outputUsage / latency` (or equivalent), consistent with Dashboard TPS widgets. ## Actual behavior Column is blank / renders `undefined` for generations that clearly have output tokens and latency. ## Root cause (source in `v3.205.1`) File: [`web/src/components/table/use-cases/observations.tsx`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/v3.205.1/web/src/components/table/use-cases/observations.tsx) Row mapping writes the new usage shape: ```ts usage: { inputUsage: generation.inputUsage, outputUsage: generation.outputUsage, totalUsage: generation.totalUsage, } ``` But the Tokens per second cell still reads the old fields: ```ts const usage: { promptTokens: number; completionTokens: number; totalTokens: number; } = row.getValue("usage"); return latency !== undefined && (usage.completionTokens !== 0 || usage.totalTokens !== 0) ? ( {usage.completionTokens && latency ? Number((usage.completionTokens / latency).toFixed(1)) : undefined} ) : undefined; ``` `completionTokens` / `totalTokens` are never set on the row, so the expression always evaluates to `undefined`. Nearby columns already use the correct fields (`outputUsage` / `inputUsage` / `totalUsage`), which is why Output Tokens can show while Tokens per second does not. This looks like a leftover from [#3511](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/3511) (original Tokens per second column) aft

title: bug: eval preview tables run unbounded full-history ClickHouse queries, can exhaust memory
body:
### Describe the bug

When setting up an LLM-as-a-Judge / evaluator (`/evals/new`), the "Sample over the last 24 hours that match filters" preview is supposed to be time-bounded, but the underlying ClickHouse query has **no time filter at all**. It sorts the project's entire observation/trace history to return a handful of preview rows.

On large self-hosted projects this can OOM ClickHouse. The query that failed for us (comment `getObservationsTableInternal`) had only `project_id`, `type` and `environment` in its `WHERE`, then `ORDER BY toDate(start_time) DESC, start_time DESC`:

```
Code: 241. DB::Exception: (total) memory limit exceeded: would use 15.41 GiB
(attempt to allocate chunk of 6523591 bytes), current RSS: 18.92 GiB, maximum: 18.90 GiB.
OvercommitTracker decision: Query was selected to stop by OvercommitTracker:
While executing MergingSortedTransform. (MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)
(comment: {"kind":"rows","feature":"tracing","type":"observation",
"operation_name":"getObservationsTableInternal"})
```

**Root cause**: `ObservationsTable`, `TracesTable` and the v4 `EventsTable` all compute
`const filterState = externalFilterState || combinedFilterState;`. When the eval preview passes an `externalFilterState`, this **replaces** the whole combined filter state — including the 24h `dateRangeFilter`, which only lives inside `combinedFilterState`. So the `externalDateRange={last1Day}` the preview also passes is silently dropped, and both `generations.all` and `generations.countAll` scan the full history.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Self-host with a project that has a large observation history.
2. Go to `Evaluators → Set up evaluator`, target Observations/Traces.
3. Observe the preview table. The `generations.all` / `generations.countAll` tRPC payloads carry no `startTime >=` filter, and the ClickHouse query sorts the entire project history.

Langfuse Cloud

title: bug(self-hosting): v4 backfill background migrations fail with TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED — fired chunk queries inherit a hardcoded 35s max_execution_time, contradicting the fire-and-poll design
body:
## Describe the bug

The v4 preparation background migrations (`20260701_v4_step_1..4`, enabled via `LANGFUSE_BACKGROUND_MIGRATION_V4_ENABLE_HISTORIC_BACKFILL=true`) fail on self-hosted deployments whose ClickHouse cannot finish a monthly-partition chunk in under **35 seconds**. Every large chunk dies server-side with:

```
Code: 159. DB::Exception: Timeout exceeded: elapsed 36448.796263 ms, maximum: 35000 ms. (TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED)
```

The backfill runner is explicitly designed for long-running queries — `fireQuery` in `worker/src/backgroundMigrations/utils/backfillBase.ts` fires the INSERT with a server-side `query_id`, **aborts the HTTP connection so the query continues server-side**, and polls `system.processes` / `system.query_log` for completion. But the fired query inherits the shared ClickHouse client's derived execution cap, so ClickHouse kills it at 35s regardless of the fire-and-poll intent.

## Root cause

In `packages/shared/src/server/clickhouse/client.ts`:

```ts
const CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
const CLICKHOUSE_SERVER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_SECONDS = 5;
// ...
max_execution_time: Math.ceil(requestTimeout / 1000) + CLICKHOUSE_SERVER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_SECONDS,
```

`fireQuery` calls `commandClickhouse` without a `request_timeout` and its per-query `clickhouse_settings` (`{ ...retrySetting }`) never override `max_execution_time`, so the client-level `max_execution_time = 30 + 5 = 35s` applies to the fired chunk query. Aborting the HTTP connection does not help — the cap is a server-side query setting.

Neither the migration `args` (only `concurrency` / `pollIntervalMs` / `maxRetries` / `partitions` are read) nor any env var can raise it. The retry ladder (`max_block_size` reductions, `max_threads: 1`) makes the query *slower*, so retries time out even harder. Verified identical code on `v3.212.0` and current `main`.

This presumably never shows on Langfuse Cloud because your clusters finish monthly-partition chunks in <35s. Self-hosters on m

body:
### Describe the bug

Generation input and output emitted by `@langfuse/vercel-ai-sdk` with AI SDK v7 are stored correctly, but their cells appear blank in the classic **Tracing → Observations** table. This is a display/formatting issue, not missing telemetry: the Langfuse Public API returns both fields populated.

### Confirmed root cause: `parts` is parsed but only `content` is rendered

AI SDK's OpenTelemetry integration emits GenAI semantic-convention messages in this shape:

```ts
{
  role: "assistant",
  parts: [{ type: "text", content: "..." }]
}
```

The classic table passes this data through `toCompactVerbosityChatML`. `SimpleChatMlArraySchema` is permissive, so `{ role, parts }` is accepted successfully. After parsing, however, the formatter only serializes:

```ts
lastMessage.content
```

For AI SDK messages, `content` is undefined because the payload uses `parts`. The formatter therefore returns a successful compact result with `data: null`, producing a blank table cell instead of displaying `parts` or falling back to the raw JSON representation.

This also explains why:

- Tool observations using plain JSON display correctly.
- The Public API contains the generation input/output.
- Langfuse Cloud Fast Preview displays the same `{ role, parts }` payload correctly, because it uses a different events-table rendering path.

**Expected:** The compact formatter displays `message.content ?? message.parts`.

**Actual:** Generation rows such as `chat gemini-3.5-flash` show blank Input and Output cells when their messages use `parts`.

title: Allow annotation queues without score configs for corrected-output workflows
body:
### Problem

Annotation queues currently require at least one score config when they are created through the UI, public API, or MCP.

This prevents using an annotation queue exclusively as a corrected-output workflow: assigning traces or observations to annotators so they can review and provide corrected outputs without also defining a score. Correction scores are already designed not to carry a `configId`, so requiring a score config on the queue is unnecessary for this workflow.

### Proposed behavior

Allow annotation queues to be created with no score configs:

- accept an empty `scoreConfigIds` array
- optionally default an omitted `scoreConfigIds` field to an empty array where applicable
- keep validating every supplied score config ID as today
- keep the existing behavior unchanged for queues that do use score configs

### Use case

A team wants to create a queue, assign items to reviewers, and collect only corrected outputs. No numeric, categorical, boolean, or text score is needed.

I would be happy to contribute a focused PR with tests if this direction makes sense.

body:
### Describe the bug

When accessing a self-hosted Langfuse instance from another device on the same LAN, the frontend fails to load on certain browsers with a client-side exception.

title: fix(web): strip ASCII control characters in stripBasePath
body:
## Bug: `stripBasePath` does not strip ASCII control characters

### Problem

`getSafeRedirectPath` in [web/src/utils/redirect.ts](web/src/utils/redirect.ts) was hardened in PR #14870 to strip ASCII control characters (0x00-0x1F and 0x7F) before downstream URL handling. The sibling function `stripBasePath` in the same file still does not strip them.

`stripBasePath` is called on user-influenced paths in four production callers:

- `web/src/components/layouts/app-layout/hooks/useAuthGuard.ts:93,112` — strips `asPath` / `redirectUrl` before they become `?targetPath=` query params in the sign-in redirect.
- `web/src/components/trace/TracePage.tsx:73` — strips `router.asPath` before display.
- `web/src/components/error-page.tsx:29` — strips `router.asPath` before display.
- `web/src/ee/features/in-app-agent/components/InAppAgentMessage.tsx:108` — strips `parsedUrl.pathname` before display.

### Threat model

In `useAuthGuard.ts`, `stripBasePath(rawPath)` produces a value that is then `encodeURIComponent`-encoded into a `?targetPath=...` query parameter. The redirect URL is then returned to the browser. If `rawPath` contains `\r\n` (CRLF), `encodeURIComponent` produces `%0D%0A`, which a sufficiently old or non-strict downstream URL parser may decode back to a literal CRLF in the redirect Location header, enabling HTTP response splitting or open-redirect through legacy URL handling.

This is the same threat model that PR #14870 addressed for `getSafeRedirectPath`. The fix should be applied to the sibling function for symmetry.

### Current behavior

`stripBasePath` does not strip control characters. The paths it receives from `asPath` (the raw browser URL) or from incoming `redirectUrl` query parameters can contain:
- `\n` (0x0A) — newline
- `\r` (0x0D) — carriage return
- `\t` (0x09) — tab
- `\0` (0x00) — null byte
- `\x7F` (0x7F) — DEL

A path like `/base\n/evil` becomes `/base\n/evil` after stripping — and that string flows into log lines, breadcrumbs, and (in the auth

title: Document and pin `getColumnId` tolerance contract
body:
## Summary

`web/src/features/filters/hooks/useFilterState.ts:213-219` contains the only
LLM-tolerance layer between the LLM-generated filter columns flowing into the
URL `encodeDelimitedArray` step and the strict `tableCols[table]` registry:

```ts
function getColumnId(table: TableName, name: string): string | undefined {
  // TODO: make this more robust, will change with new filters
  // to give more leeway to LLMs, we check against name or id
  return tableCols[table]?.find((col) => col.name === name || col.id === name)
    ?.id;
}
```

The TODO has lived there for a while and the contract is **undocumented**:

- Whether lookups are scoped to one table (i.e. a column defined only in
  `observationsTableCols` cannot be resolved through `traces`).
- Whether case-sensitivity and whitespace-normalization are expected.
- Whether the matching is intended to be idempotent (id-based vs name-based).

There is also no test pinning any of these invariants, so the next refactor of
the filters system can silently regress the LLM-tolerance contract.

bug(sdk-python): OpenAI stream helpers reject Langfuse-specific arguments
body:
## Describe the bug

The Langfuse OpenAI integration accepts wrapper-specific arguments such as `langfuse_prompt` on `create()` and `parse()`, but OpenAI's higher-level `stream()` helpers reject the same arguments before the instrumented inner `create(stream=True)` call is reached.

This is not limited to the legacy beta path. It affects the current stable Chat Completions and Responses stream helpers, in both sync and async clients.

With `langfuse==4.14.0` and `openai==2.29.0`, the affected calls fail with:

```text
Completions.stream() got an unexpected keyword argument 'langfuse_prompt'
AsyncCompletions.stream() got an unexpected keyword argument 'langfuse_prompt'
Responses.stream() got an unexpected keyword argument 'langfuse_prompt'
AsyncResponses.stream() got an unexpected keyword argument 'langfuse_prompt'
```

The same root cause applies to the other Langfuse-only arguments handled by `OpenAiArgsExtractor`, including `name`, `langfuse_public_key`, `trace_id`, and `parent_observation_id`.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from langfuse import get_client
from langfuse.openai import OpenAI

langfuse = get_client()
prompt = langfuse.get_prompt("example-prompt")
client = OpenAI()

with client.chat.completions.stream(
    model="sample-model",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    langfuse_prompt=prompt,
) as stream:
    for event in stream:

title: Bug: Traces page stuck on "Configure Tracing" onboarding in events_only mode (hasTracingConfigured is not events-aware)
body:
### Summary

On a self-hosted **v4 preview** instance running in `events_only` write mode, the Tracing page permanently shows the **"Configure Tracing" / "Waiting for first trace"** onboarding screen, even though observations are ingested correctly and are fully queryable. The onboarding gate (`traces.hasTracingConfigured`) is not events-aware.

### Environment

- Self-hosted Langfuse **v3.205.1 EE** (v4 self-hosting preview)
- `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE=events_only`
- `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_ALLOW_PREVIEW_OPT_IN=true`
- `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_NATIVE_OTEL_BEHAVIOUR=direct`
- Python SDK v4 ingestion

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a self-hosted instance with `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE=events_only`.
2. Ingest traces/observations via Python SDK v4 into a fresh project (i.e. `projects.has_traces = false` and the legacy ClickHouse `traces` table is empty).
3. Open the project's Tracing page.

### Expected

The observations-first table shows the ingested observations.

### Actual

The page shows the "Configure Tracing" onboarding, hiding the data.

### Evidence that the data IS there

- tRPC `events.all` returns the observations (200 with data).
- `GET /api/public/v2/observations` returns the observations.
- The Home dashboard shows correct Traces/Observations counts.
- Only tRPC `traces.hasTracingConfigured` returns `false`, which is what triggers the onboarding screen.

### Root cause

`hasTracingConfigured` -> `hasAnyTrace(projectId)` checks:

1. the Postgres `projects.has_traces` flag, then
2. `SELECT 1 FROM traces WHERE project_id = {projectId} LIMIT 1` against the **legacy ClickHouse `traces` table**.

In `events_only` mode nothing is ever written to the legacy `traces` table, so this query always returns empty, `has_traces` never gets flipped to `true`, and `hasTracingConfigured` stays `false` forever — regardless of how many observations exist in the events tables. This is a v3-era check that was not migrated to be events-aware.

title: bug: Session "Total cost" shows $0.00 when cost is model-calculated (not caller-ingested)
body:
## Describe the bug On the Sessions page, the header shows `Total cost: $0.00`, while `Total traces: 27`
in the same header is correct. Cost is present at every other layer — only the
session-level cost rollup returns 0. Setup: Langfuse Cloud (Hobby). Cost is not caller-provided — the app sends token
usage only, and Langfuse derives cost from the model price table (Langfuse-managed
model definitions match). ## Where cost is / isn't visible A single session, 27 traces / 259 observations: | Layer | Cost | | -- | -- | | Individual trace detail | shown ✅ | | `GET /api/public/traces?sessionId=…` (per-trace `totalCost`) | populated on all 27 ✅ | | Metrics API — `sum(totalCost)`, `view=traces`, filter `sessionId` | correct ✅ | | Metrics API — `sum(totalCost)`, `view=observations`, filter `sessionId` | correct (259 obs) ✅ | | Sessions page header — "Total cost" | $0.00 ❌ | Persists after refresh (not ingestion lag). The trace count in the same header is
correct, so the session aggregate ran — it just summed an empty cost source. ## Likely root cause At the observation level: * `totalCost` (caller-ingested) = `null` * `calculatedTotalCost` (Langfuse-derived from price table) = populated The metrics/dashboard engine sums the resolved value (ingested → else calculated)
and is correct. The sessions rollup appears to sum the raw ingested cost column,
which is `null` here, yielding $0.00. So it surfaces specifically when cost is model-calculated rather than caller-provided.
Callers passing explicit `cost_details` likely don't hit it. ## Expected Sessions "Total cost" should equal the sum of the session's trace/observation costs,
matching the Metrics API and trace-detail views — regardless of ingested vs calculated. ## Related Same $0.00 rollup class on other surfaces: langfuse/langfuse#10322 (dataset-run), [#2596](), langfuse/langfu

title: bug: scores.all fails with ClickHouse NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK on ClickHouse 26.x (FINAL + LEFT JOIN + new analyzer)
body:
### Describe the bug

Opening the Scores table in the UI (tRPC route `scores.all`) returns a 500. The
underlying ClickHouse query fails at planning time with:

```
Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column
and(equals(__table1.project_id, 'x'_String),
    in(__table1.data_type, __set_String_...),
    notIn(__table1.environment, __set_LowCardinality(String)_...),
    greaterOrEquals(__table1.timestamp, _CAST(...)),
    lessOrEquals(__table1.timestamp, _CAST(...)))
: in block __table1.id String String(size = 0), __table1.project_id ...,
  ... ingestion_api_key ..., ingestion_sdk_name ..., ingestion_sdk_version ....
(NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) (version 26.6.1.1193 (official build))
```

This is **not** a missing/un-migrated column — the block header in the error
lists every column, including `ingestion_api_key` / `ingestion_sdk_name` /
`ingestion_sdk_version` and `metadata`. It is a ClickHouse **new-analyzer
regression** that fires when three things coincide:

1. the new analyzer (default in ClickHouse 26.x),
2. `FINAL` on the left table, and
3. a `LEFT JOIN`.

The `scores.all` query is exactly that shape —
`packages/shared/src/server/repositories/scores.ts` (`getScoresUiGeneric`):

```sql
SELECT ...
FROM scores s final
LEFT JOIN traces t ON s.trace_id = t.id AND t.project_id = s.project_id
WHERE s.project_id = {projectId} AND s.data_type IN (...) AND <filters>
ORDER BY ... LIMIT ... OFFSET ...
```

The JOIN is always present for the rows path (`performTracesJoin` is true when
`select: "rows"`).

Expected: the Scores table loads. Actual: 500 / `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`.

### Steps to reproduce

Data-independent — reproduces with a non-existent `project_id`, so it fails at
query planning. Against a ClickHouse 26.6.1 instance with the Langfuse schema:

```sql
SELECT s.id, s.project_id, s.environment, s.value, s.timestamp, s.data_type,
       s.ingestion_sdk_name, s.ingestion_sdk_version, s.is_deleted, s.event_ts,
       t.user_id
FROM scores s final
LEFT JOIN traces t O

title: bug: GPT-5.6 Sol totalCost ignores cached input, reasoning, and cache-write premium
body:
### Customer impact

GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna observations can persist pricing-relevant usage buckets that their default pricing entries do not recognize. In particular, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` are stored but currently receive no default price. Explicit cache-write buckets are also not represented.

The reported Sol sample stores:

```json
{
  "input": 786,
  "cache_read_input_tokens": 718398,
  "output": 242,
  "reasoning_tokens": 25
}
```

Only `input` and `output` are currently priced, materially understating cost for cache-heavy requests. Pylon #4622 reports roughly a 2x aggregate undercount.

### Root cause

The GPT-5.6 entries contain normalized aliases such as `input_cached_tokens`, `input_cache_read`, `output_reasoning_tokens`, and `output_reasoning`, but not the raw keys present in the customer's stored `usageDetails`. Price matching is exact by usage key.

### Intended solution

Update all existing Standard and Large Context (>272K) tiers for GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna:

* map `cache_read_input_tokens` to the existing cached-input rate;
* map `reasoning_tokens` to the existing output/reasoning rate;
* price explicit `input_cache_creation` and `cache_write_tokens` buckets at the provider-confirmed 1.25x input rate;
* add a regression test using the reported usage shape.

### Scope and non-goals

* Do not add implicit-cache-write pricing tiers.
* Do not reinterpret ordinary `input` as cache-write usage when no explicit write bucket exists.
* Preserve the existing Standard and Large Context tier selection.
* Historical cost recomputation/backfill is out of scope and requires a separate decision.

For the reported payload, the defensible forward-looking correction is $0.738273 from explicit stored buckets. The additional implicit write premium in the originally reported $0.740238 cannot be inferred safely from this payload.

When using LangChain's `SystemMessage(content_blocks=[{"type": "text", "text": "..."}])` (which produces a `list`-type `message.content`), the Langfuse server stores the observation's `input[0].content` field as a **Python `str()` repr string** (with single quotes) instead of preserving the JSON array structure.

This means in the Langfuse UI and API, the system prompt appears as:
```
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'You are a test agent.\n\n# Role\n\n...'}]
```
Instead of either a plain Markdown string or a proper JSON array with double quotes.

title: bug(sdk-python): Failed OTEL media uploads with openinference
body:
### Describe the bug

When generating an image with Gemini, openinference will return the base64 in both the message parts and the final output.value field within the OTEL span.

Langfuse will attempt to upload both, which is fine, since the second upload would normally cancel automatically.

However, one of the images is actually urlsafe base64, which results in the invalid strings "-" and "_" to be dropped.
This causes two possible scenarios:
* Two separate medias are uploaded, one being the correct image, the other being an empty/failed image
* The resulting string is not %4 length, which results in an error, and the output value is replaced with an error message instead of the Langfuse media tag


While this could be considered an issue with the openinference, since that package is the recommended by Langfuse it would seem appropriate to handle this on the SDK side.

My suggestion would be to modify the following section to accept urlsafe base64:

title: bug: silent wrong results in two score-analytics aggregations (histogram binning & pivot-table averages)
body:
## Summary

While differential-testing Langfuse's client-side statistical code against reference libraries (`numpy`, `scikit-learn`), I found two **silent** correctness bugs — they return wrong numbers to users with no error, on the dashboards people use to read eval results:

1. **Numeric score histogram** (`createHistogramData`) counts scores in the **wrong bucket**, because it rounds each value to 2 decimals *before* binning. The rendered distribution disagrees with a standard histogram, and buckets are labeled with ranges that don't contain the values counted in them.
2. **Pivot-table subtotals/grand totals** (`calculateSubtotals`) compute averages as an **average of per-group averages** instead of a count-weighted average, so subtotal/total rows overstate or understate metrics like avg cost/latency whenever groups differ in size.

Both live in correctness-critical analytics paths. I've verified the neighbouring inter-rater stats (`calculateCohensKappa`, `calculateWeightedF1Score`, `calculateOverallAgreement`) against scikit-learn and they are **correct** (0 mismatches over 1,200 random cases) — these two are the outliers.

---

## Bug 1 — Numeric score histogram bins on rounded values

**File:** `web/src/features/dashboard/lib/score-analytics-utils.ts` → `createHistogramData` (rendered by the dashboard `NumericScoreHistogram`, produced in `dashboard-router.ts`).

The value is rounded to 2 decimals before its bin index is computed, while the bin edges are not:

```ts
const min = round(Math.min(...numericScoreValues));            // rounded
const binSize = range / bins || 1;
// ...
const shiftedValue = round(value) - min;                       // value rounded to 2dp
const binIndex = Math.min(Math.floor(shiftedValue / binSize), bins - 1);
```

### Reproduction (vs `numpy.histogram`)

A faithful port of the function was run against `numpy.histogram` (same bin count) over 1,200 random score datasets:

```
uniform 0..1 (n=50)          | value-in-wrong-bucket:185/200

title: bug: Malformed timestamp query param crashes trace/peek views
body:
## Problem

Trace detail and table-peek views parse the `timestamp` URL query param with bare `new Date(decodeURIComponent(...))`. A malformed percent-encoded value (for example `?timestamp=%`) throws `URIError` and can crash the React tree. Invalid date strings become `Invalid Date` and are passed through inconsistently.

## Motivation

Self-hosted and shared links sometimes carry a corrupted or hand-edited `timestamp` query param. The page should degrade to the existing no-timestamp lookup path instead of throwing.

## Background

Eval preview navigation already guards this in a private `parseTimestamp` helper (`web/src/features/evals/hooks/useEvalPreviewNavigation.ts`): array check, try/catch around `decodeURIComponent`, and `Number.isNaN(date.getTime())`. Peek views and the standalone trace page still use the unsafe pattern. PR #12796 added decoding for peek observation detail but did not add validation.

## Current behavior

- Malformed encoding (`%`) → `URIError` (uncaught)
- Non-date string → `Invalid Date` passed to data hooks
- Array query values are not handled consistently across call sites

## Expected behavior

Parse failures return `undefined` so callers keep the existing no-timestamp code path (correct results; slightly less partition pruning).

## Proposed solution

Extract a shared `parseTraceTimestampFromQuery()` utility matching the eval-preview helper, and use it in:

- `peek-trace-detail.tsx`
- `peek-observation-detail.tsx`
- `peek-experiment-item-detail.tsx`
- `pages/project/[projectId]/traces/[traceId].tsx`
- optionally reuse from `useEvalPreviewNavigation.ts`

Add client unit tests for valid, encoded, malformed, invalid, array, and empty inputs.

## Alternatives considered

- Leave call sites as-is and rely on well-formed links only — still crashes on bad URLs
- Show an error toast on parse failure — heavier UX for a recoverable query param

## Scope

- Client-side query parsing only
- No API, schema, or ClickHouse query changes

title: bug(sdk-python): empty-string credentials silently bypass auth-disable guard; malformed media reference string crashes with raw unpack error
body:
Found while doing a testing/error-handling audit of the Python SDK. Two related input-validation gaps, both reproducible on current `main`:

## 1. Empty-string `public_key`/`secret_key` bypasses the "client disabled" guard

`Langfuse.__init__` checks for missing credentials like this:

```python
public_key = public_key or os.environ.get(LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY)
if public_key is None:
    langfuse_logger.warning("... Client will be disabled ...")
    self._otel_tracer = otel_trace_api.NoOpTracer()
    return
```

If `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` is set to `""` (a real scenario: a templated Docker/k8s env file rendering an unset secret as an empty string), `public_key or os.environ.get(...)` evaluates to `""`, which is **not** `None`. The guard is skipped, and the SDK proceeds to build a fully-wired `Tracer` and resource manager as if it had valid credentials. The failure only surfaces later as an opaque auth/404 error on the first real request, instead of the clean, immediate "client will be disabled" warning the SDK is designed to give.

Repro:
```python
import os
os.environ["LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY"] = ""
os.environ["LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY"] = "sk-test"
from langfuse import Langfuse
lf = Langfuse()
print(type(lf._otel_tracer).__name__)  # "Tracer", not "NoOpTracer"
print(lf._resources)  # a real LangfuseResourceManager, not None
```

Same issue applies to `secret_key`, and to passing `public_key=""` directly as a constructor argument when the env var is also unset.

**Fix:** check falsiness (`if not public_key:`) instead of identity (`if public_key is None:`) for both keys.

## 2. `LangfuseMedia.parse_reference_string` crashes on a malformed pipe-separated segment

```python
content = reference_string[len("@@@langfuseMedia:"):].rstrip("@@@")
pairs = content.split("|")
parsed_data = {}
for pair in pairs:
    key, value = pair.split("=", 1)  # <-- crashes if pair has no "="
    parsed_data[key] = value
```

The method otherwise validates its input carefully and raises clean `ValueError

title: bug(otel): structured gen_ai.system_instructions render as [object Object]
body:
### Describe the bug

## Context

Support for prepending `gen_ai.system_instructions` was introduced in [PR #12442](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/12442). That change supports both `pydantic_ai.all_messages` and the generic `gen_ai.input.messages` path and intentionally avoids adding another system message when the input already contains one.

The current implementation assumes an instruction array contains individual instruction parts. For each array element, it reads a truthy `content` property or falls back to JavaScript string coercion.

Complete messages shaped as `{ role: "system", parts: [...] }` have no top-level `content`, so the fallback evaluates `String(message)`. JavaScript converts an object this way to `"[object Object]"`, causing silent loss of the system instructions.

This shape is emitted by LiteLLM rather than being manually constructed by the Langfuse caller:

- LiteLLM documents `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, and `gen_ai.system_instructions` as JSON-encoded arrays of `{role, parts: [...]}` objects in its [OpenTelemetry attributes reference](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/observability/opentelemetry_integration#attributes-reference).
- Its upstream test passes a complete `role: "system"` message as `system_instructions` and verifies that the serialized OTEL attribute retains the system role and contains `parts`: [LiteLLM OpenTelemetry test](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/301a02b7bede045053352555f1c57f3fd25dd387/tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_opentelemetry.py#L4059-L4075).

title: perf: span_processor.on_end evaluates span_formatter(span) eagerly via f-string regardless of log level
body:
### Summary

`LangfuseSpanProcessor.on_end` in `langfuse/_client/span_processor.py` evaluates `span_formatter(span)` eagerly inside an f-string passed to `langfuse_logger.debug(...)`. Because Python f-strings are evaluated *before* being handed to the logger, the full span serialization runs on **every** span end, regardless of the effective log level. This is a measurable per-span CPU cost on the thread that ends the span (in async apps, the event loop thread), and cannot be mitigated by raising the log level.

### Environment

- Langfuse Python SDK: `langfuse-python` 4.14.0 (also confirmed still present on `main` as of 2026-07-23)
- Python 3.12
- OS: Linux (containerized, FastAPI + asyncio)

### Reproducible example

The offending code (current `main`, `langfuse/_client/span_processor.py`, `LangfuseSpanProcessor.on_end`):

```python
langfuse_logger.debug(
    f"Trace: Processing span name='{span._name}' | Full details:\n{span_formatter(span)}"
)
```

`span_formatter(span)` performs a full `json.dumps` of the span (attributes, events, links, resource, instrumentationScope). Profiling a decorated async handler returning ~1000 spans/s shows this single call at ~0.27 ms/span, i.e. ~27% of one core purely on formatting a debug message that is never emitted (logger at WARNING).

Crucially, setting `LANGFUSE_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` (or `debug=False`) does **not** help: the f-string is constructed before `logger.debug` is called, so the formatting cost is paid unconditionally.

### Root cause

Python logging defers %-formatting of *arguments* (via `logger.debug(msg, *args)`), but it cannot defer evaluation of expressions already embedded in an f-string. The f-string is built at call time, so `span_formatter(span)` runs even when the DEBUG level is disabled. This is the well-known f-string-in-logging anti-pattern (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54367975).

### Impact

- Per-span overhead on the calling thread (event loop in async apps) → contributes to GIL pressure under h

title: bug: observation panel drops the reasoning block when completion is an empty string
body:
**Describe the bug**

On a generation whose output object is `{"completion": "", "reasoning": "..."}`, the observation panel's pretty view renders only the `completion` row (an empty string) and omits the reasoning block entirely. The identical shape with a non-empty `completion` renders the reasoning block as expected.

The data itself is intact: fetching the same trace via the public API returns the full reasoning string, so this is purely a rendering issue in the observation panel.

**To reproduce**

1. Ingest a generation observation whose output is `{"completion": "", "reasoning": "some model reasoning text"}`. This shape occurs naturally with reasoning models that produce a reasoning trace but deliberately emit no assistant text (for example a considered "stay silent" turn in a multi-participant chat, routed via OpenRouter).
2. Open the observation in the UI.
3. The pretty view shows a one-row key/value table (`completion: ""`) with no reasoning block. Toggling the output block to JSON view reveals the full object including `reasoning`, which is the current workaround.

**Expected behavior**

The reasoning block renders whenever `reasoning` is present, regardless of whether `completion` is an empty string. Empty completion plus populated reasoning is a legitimate and increasingly common output shape for reasoning models.

**Possible cause**

The symptom pattern (non-empty completion shows reasoning, empty string hides it) suggests a truthiness check on `completion` gating the rich assistant/reasoning renderer, with a fallback to the plain table when the string is falsy.

**Environment**

Self-hosted Langfuse v3.204.0 (web + worker), traces ingested through an OpenRouter broadcast integration. Also checked release notes up to v3.224.0 and open issues for a duplicate; the existing reasoning-related items concern request options, pricing, and Bedrock parsing, not this rendering path.

title: bug: unclustered multi-ALTER migrations fail with CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER (517) on ClickHouse Cloud, leaving schema_migrations dirty
body:
### Describe the bug

Startup ClickHouse migrations that issue **multiple ALTERs on the same table** intermittently fail on **ClickHouse Cloud** with:

```
Code: 517. DB::Exception: Looks like this replica doesn't catchup with latest ALTER query updates:
metadata version on replica is 14, while common metadata is 15. Please retry this query. (CANNOT_ASSIGN_ALTER)
```

golang-migrate does not retry (ClickHouse explicitly asks for a retry), so it marks `schema_migrations` dirty and the web container exits. Every subsequent boot then fails fast with:

```
error: Dirty database version 35. Fix and force version.
Applying clickhouse migrations failed. Common causes: ...
Exiting...
```

→ `langfuse-web` CrashLoopBackOff until the dirty flag is cleared manually. In our case this turned a routine pod restart into a multi-day outage: the dirty flag was left behind by a failed upgrade attempt, the running pod kept serving, and the next unrelated restart (an RDS maintenance window) hit the dirty flag and crash-looped.

#13398 (merged 2026-04-29) fixed exactly this by adding `SETTINGS alter_sync = 2` / `mutations_sync = 2` per statement — **but only in `clustered/`**, on the assumption that "`unclustered/` runs against plain MergeTree where both settings are documented no-ops."

That assumption doesn't hold: the [self-hosting docs for ClickHouse Cloud](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/infrastructure/clickhouse) prescribe `CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER_ENABLED=false`, which selects the **unclustered** migrations — executed against **SharedMergeTree**, where the metadata catch-up race is real. So ClickHouse Cloud + the documented configuration is precisely the unprotected combination.

Concretely, at v3.221.1: `clustered/0035_add_ingestion_attribution_columns.up.sql` carries `SETTINGS alter_sync = 2` on each of its three ALTERs, while the `unclustered/` twin carries none. Some unclustered files (0012–0018, 0033) do already carry the settings, so the tree is currently inconsistent.

body:
### Describe the bug

## Summary

When a `Langfuse` client is configured with the `mask` hook, spans emitted by third-party OpenTelemetry instrumentation (OpenLIT, OpenInference instrumentors, etc.) are exported **without any masking applied**, while native Langfuse observations are masked correctly. There is no runtime warning, and the framework integration docs that recommend wiring instrumentors into the Langfuse tracer do not mention this, so users can reasonably believe their masking covers everything when it silently does not.

I understand this is by design: the masking docs state that `mask` transforms data at SDK attribute-creation time and does not inspect raw OTel span attributes, and `mask_otel_spans` (export-stage) is the documented recommendation for that case. The problem is that the failure mode is **silent** and the discoverability is poor: nothing in the `mask` path or in the integration guides (e.g. Agno via `openlit.init(tracer=langfuse._otel_tracer, ...)`) signals that `mask` will not cover those spans. For applications handling regulated data (in our case, privileged legal documents under Brazilian LGPD), this is a PII-leak footgun.

## Expected behavior

One of:
- `mask` also applies to third-party spans flowing through the Langfuse span processor, or
- a clear runtime warning when `mask` is configured and non-SDK spans are exported without `mask_otel_spans`, or
- at minimum, an explicit callout in the masking docs and in each third-party integration guide.

## Actual behavior

Native observation content is masked; third-party span attributes (`input.value`, `llm.input_messages.0.message.content`, ...) reach the exporter with their original content. No warning is emitted.

title: feat(public-api): add DELETE /api/public/comments/{commentId} endpoint
body:
## Problem

The public REST API for comments supports `POST /api/public/comments` and `GET /api/public/comments[/{commentId}]`, but it has no `DELETE` endpoint. Every other commentable resource exposed over the public API already does — `DELETE /api/public/traces/{traceId}`, `DELETE /api/public/scores/{scoreId}`, `DELETE /api/public/observations/{observationId}` (via bulk) — so the omission here breaks the symmetry API users expect.

The corresponding tRPC mutation (`comments.delete`) exists in `web/src/server/api/routers/comments.ts`, and the underlying Prisma delete path is exercised by the UI today. The public API just doesn't surface it.

## Motivation

Two real user-facing consequences:

1. **API parity.** A user creating a comment via the public API has no clean way to remove it without dropping into the UI or scripting the tRPC route. That makes the public API a write-only path for comments.
2. **Symmetry with `POST /api/public/comments`.** Today the public API can author comments but cannot retract them. For moderation / redaction workflows (PII that landed in a comment, an accidentally-shared session id, etc.) the only workaround is direct DB access.

## Current behavior

- `DELETE /api/public/comments/{commentId}` returns `404` from the Next.js page router (the file only registers a `GET` handler).
- The public Fern definition (`fern/apis/server/definition/comments.yml`) lists only `create`, `get`, and `get-by-id` for the `/comments` resource.
- The generated `web/public/generated/api/openapi.yml` reflects the same gap.

## Expected behavior

- Return `200` with `{ "message": "Comment deleted successfully" }` on success, matching the `trace-delete` shape.

title: feat(admin-api): List all organizations belonging to a user by email
body:
## Feature Request (open to contribute)

### Description
Add a new admin API endpoint that allows listing all organizations belonging to a user based on their email address, including their organization-level permissions.

### Current Problem
Currently, there is no direct way to retrieve organizations for a specific user via email. This forces workflows to:
1. Pull all organizations from the system
2. Iterate through each organization to check if the user belongs to it
3. Check the user's permission level within each organization

This approach results in unnecessary API calls and poor performance, especially in self-hosted deployments with many organizations. It creates a significant bottleneck for automation workflows and internal tooling that needs to verify user org membership and permissions.

### Use Cases
1. **User Provisioning Workflows**: Enable administrators to programmatically retrieve which organizations a user is a member of for user management in self-hosted deployments.

2. **Organization Membership Auditing**: Facilitate auditing and verification of user membership across organizations.

3. **Internal Identity Integration**: Allow integration with internal identity/account management systems for automated user administration.

4. **Project Provisioning Automation**: Enable org admins to automate provisioning of projects via workflows and internal tools. The endpoint should include organization-level permissions so that callers can verify if a user is an admin at the organization level, enabling conditional automation workflows (e.g., only org admins can trigger project creation workflows).

### Proposed Solution
Add a new admin API endpoint:
- **Endpoint**: `GET /api/admin/users/{email}/organizations` or similar
- **Authentication**: Requires admin API key

- **Parameters**: User email address
- **Response**: List of organizations the user belongs to with metadata including:
  - Organization ID, name
  - User's role/permission level within the organ

title: bug: code evaluator docs show `data_type`/`dataType` as equivalent, but a plain dict return requires camelCase in both languages
body:
### Describe the bug

The [code evaluators docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators) present `data_type` (Python) / `dataType` (TypeScript) as the correct per-language casing, and the Python example reinforces this via a `Score` dataclass with a `data_type: str` field. But `evaluate()` can also return a plain dict, and for a plain dict the runtime requires `dataType` even in Python — `data_type` fails at evaluation time with `INVALID_RESULT`, not at evaluator creation time. The docs don't note that the casing is conditional on how the score object is constructed.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a `code` evaluator (`POST /api/public/unstable/evaluators`) whose Python source returns a plain dict:

```python
def evaluate(ctx: EvaluationContext) -> EvaluationResult:
    return {
        "scores": [
            {"name": "example", "value": True, "data_type": "BOOLEAN"}
        ]
    }
```

Run it via an evaluation rule. It fails with:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_RESULT",
    "message": "The evaluator returned an invalid result. Return { scores: [...] } with at least one score. Each score requires a name, dataType, and value; dataType must match the value type. See https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators for details."
  }
}
```

Changing the key to `"dataType"` (still a plain dict, still Python) resolves it.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Langfuse Cloud

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

_No response_

### SDK and integration versions

_No response_

### Additional information

Either would fix it: clarify in the docs that a plain-dict return needs `dataType` regardless of language, or have the runtime accept `data_type` as an alias on dict returns.

### Are you interested in contributing a fix for this bug?

No

title: bug(worker): worker silently stops consuming all queues after Redis lock loss (FLUSHALL / eviction) — stays 'healthy', needs manual restart
body:
## Describe the bug

When the worker loses its BullMQ job locks mid-flight (Redis `FLUSHALL`, key eviction under `volatile-lru`, or presumably failover), it enters a permanent wedged state instead of crashing:

- it stops consuming jobs from **all** queues,
- it stops emitting log lines entirely,
- but the process stays alive: the container keeps running (ECS reports the task healthy/RUNNING), and the CloudWatch queue-metrics publishing loop (`ENABLE_AWS_CLOUDWATCH_METRIC_PUBLISHING=true`) keeps publishing `langfuse.queue.*` metrics, so the deployment *looks* alive from the outside.

The only recovery is a manual container restart. Because nothing crashes and nothing goes unhealthy, orchestrator auto-restart (ECS/k8s) never triggers. In our case the wedged worker went unnoticed twice — for 2 days and then 3 days — while ingestion events accumulated in Redis until it OOMed.

## To reproduce

Self-hosted Langfuse v3 (langfuse/langfuse-worker:3) on ECS Fargate, ElastiCache Valkey 7.2 with TLS, single worker.

We have two clean reproductions:

1. **Lock eviction**: Redis at 100% memory with `maxmemory-policy=volatile-lru` evicted BullMQ lock keys (they have TTLs, so volatile-lru targets them preferentially). Worker logs show a cascade of `Missing lock for job <N>. moveToDelayed` errors, then total log silence to the exact minute. Worker never consumed another job.
2. **FLUSHALL with jobs in flight**: an operational `FLUSHALL` while the worker had active jobs produced the same cascade and the same permanent silence, immediately.

In both cases the last log lines are repeated BullMQ lock errors (`Missing lock for job N. moveToDelayed` / lock-related `moveToFailed` errors), after which the worker never logs or processes again, while the process itself keeps running.

## Expected behavior

One of:

1. **Crash-only**: if the BullMQ workers hit unrecoverable lock-loss state (e.g., a burst of `Missing lock` errors across queues, or all queue executors dead), exit the process s

title: Consider `X-Forwarded-Host` header for MCP Server
body:
## Problem Description

The Langfuse Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server validates incoming connections by inspecting the HTTP `Host` header against allowed host configurations. 

However, in many production cloud environments (such as AWS ALB, Cloudflare, Traefik, Nginx reverse proxies, or Kubernetes Ingresses), the original `Host` header is modified or replaced with the internal service name/IP address when forwarding traffic to the upstream container. Instead, standard proxy architectures relay the original client host in the **`X-Forwarded-Host`** header.

Because the MCP server currently relies solely on the `Host` header:
* Requests passing through reverse proxies/ingress controllers fail host verification.
* Operators are forced to alter standard proxy rules or hardcode host rewrites, which goes against best practices for many cloud infrastructure providers.

## Proposed Solution

Update the MCP Server's request verification logic to respect proxy headers:

1. **Fallback/Fallback order:** Inspect `X-Forwarded-Host` prior to or as a fallback to `Host` (e.g., `req.headers['x-forwarded-host'] || req.headers['host']`).
2. *(Optional / Recommended)* **Trust Proxy Setting:** If applicable (e.g., Express/Fastify backends), expose or respect standard `TRUST_PROXY` / proxy settings so header spoofing risks are mitigated when behind trusted reverse proxies.

## Additional Context & Standard References

* **RFC 7239 / De-facto Standard:** `X-Forwarded-Host` is the widely accepted standard header for identifying the original host requested by the client in HTTP proxying.
* **Impact:** Affects users deploying MCP servers in Kubernetes, AWS ECS/EKS behind ALBs, or behind Cloudflare/Traefik API gateways.

title: bug: traces table score filters aggregate every score name in the project, exhausting ClickHouse memory
body:
### Describe the bug

Filtering the Traces table by a **score value** makes `getTracesTableGeneric` build a `scores_avg` CTE that aggregates **every score name in the project**, then discards all but the filtered name in the outer `WHERE`. On projects with high score volume this CTE dominates the cost of the statement and can exhaust the ClickHouse server memory budget, taking unrelated queries down with it.

The CTE is bounded only from below:

```sql
FROM scores s FINAL
WHERE project_id = {projectId: String}
  AND s.timestamp >= {traceTimestamp: DateTime64(3)} - INTERVAL 1 HOUR   -- no upper bound
GROUP BY project_id, trace_id, name, data_type, string_value
```

The missing upper bound looks deliberate (scores can be attached long after their trace, so bounding at `toTimestamp` would drop late annotations and eval scores). The consequence is that **narrowing the UI date range barely helps** — the scan is anchored at the window start and always runs to "now". Selecting an *older* 24 h window is more expensive than a recent one.

`name`, meanwhile, is never filtered — even though it is the third column of the sort key:

```sql
ORDER BY (project_id, toDate(timestamp), name, id)
```

### Impact observed

Self-hosted, `3.185.0` and reproduced on `3.224.1`, ClickHouse 25.2 (3 replicas, 25 GiB limit → `max_server_memory_usage` 22.5 GiB), `scores` 92 GB / `observations` 480 GB.

```
Code: 241. DB::Exception: (total) memory limit exceeded: would use 12.13 GiB
(attempt to allocate chunk of 8372224 bytes), current RSS: 22.49 GiB, maximum: 22.50 GiB.
OvercommitTracker decision: Query was selected to stop by OvercommitTracker:
While executing AggregatingTransform. (MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)
(comment: {"surface":"trpc","route":"traces.countAll","projectId":"..."})
```

Failures also land on `FillingRightJoinSide` — the CTE is the build side of the `LEFT JOIN`, and hash joins have no spill path.

### Proposed fix

Restrict the CTE to the score names the filters reference. This is s

title: bug: Blob Storage export: object keys truncated to whole seconds cause silent overwrite / data loss
body:
### Describe the bug

When exporting traces via the **S3 Blob Storage Integration** (hourly schedule, Parquet), some export windows are silently written as **empty (0-row) files even though the traces for those windows exist in Langfuse** (they're returned by the API and present in ClickHouse). The export run reports success and writes a manifest, so nothing signals a problem. I expected every trace present in Langfuse to appear in the exported files for its window.

The loss is **silent and permanent**: the run succeeds, the incremental cursor advances past the window, and the window is never re-scanned. It is also effectively **undetectable downstream** — for Parquet the manifest records `rowCount: null`, so an overwritten (empty) window is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty one. On our hourly integration this silently drops ~7–8 windows/day.

### What's happening

The exporter [processes at most one `frequencyInterval` of data per run](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/main/worker/src/features/blobstorage/handleBlobStorageIntegrationProjectJob.ts#L1050-L1058), and if it is still behind the `now − lagBuffer` frontier it [immediately re-queues the next chunk](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/main/worker/src/features/blobstorage/handleBlobStorageIntegrationProjectJob.ts#L1195-L1210). So a single scheduler wake-up that is just over one interval behind emits **two chunks back-to-back**: a full-interval chunk ending at time `T`, and a sub-second "remainder" chunk ending a few milliseconds later.

The export object key for each chunk is [built from that chunk's `maxTimestamp`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/main/worker/src/features/blobstorage/handleBlobStorageIntegrationProjectJob.ts#L574-L576), but [`formatBlobExportTimestamp` truncates it to whole seconds](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/main/worker/src/features/blobstorage/manifest.ts#L27-L28) (`.substring(0, 19)`). title: bug: GET /api/public/v2/observations silently ignores the sessionId query parameter
body:
### Describe the bug

`GET /api/public/v2/observations` accepts a `sessionId` query parameter (documented under [Observations API](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/observations-api), returns `200`), but the value is never applied. The response is the project's entire observation set.

A session id that does not exist at all returns the same rows as a valid one, so there is no error and no empty result to notice — the caller silently receives unrelated data.

`sessionId` appears to be the only affected parameter. `userId` — its closest sibling, same shape, same place in the docs — filters correctly, as do `traceId`, `name`, `type`, `level`, `environment`, `isRootObservation` and `parentObservationId`. Passing the same predicate through the `filter` parameter also works, which is the workaround below.

This matters more than a normal filter bug because `sessionId` is the documented replacement path for an endpoint removed in v4: [Migration of deprecated APIs](https://langfuse.com/faq/all/deprecated-api-migration) says to replace `GET /api/public/sessions` with "`GET /v2/observations` filtered by `sessionId`". Following that instruction literally produces cross-session data.

**Expected:** `sessionId=X` returns only observations whose `sessionId` is `X`, and an unknown session id returns an empty `data` array — matching how `userId` and the `filter` equivalent already behave. If the shorthand cannot be supported, rejecting it with a `400` would at least be safe; silently widening a filter to "everything" is the one outcome a caller cannot detect.

### Steps to reproduce

No special data is needed — this reproduces on any project containing at least one session, since the fastest check is that an entirely fictional session id still returns rows.

```bash
# LF_HOST = base URL, LF_AUTH = base64 "pk-lf-...:sk-lf-..."
curl -s -H "Authorization: Basic $LF_AUTH" \
  "$LF_HOST/api/public/v2/observations?limit=200&fields=core,basic&sessionId=definitely-n

```

roughly every 90–110 seconds, indefinitely. It accounts for **~45% of the web pod's log volume**.

The **worker** container — same image, same environment variables, same mounted CA, and a much heavier Redis user — logs **zero** of these. That asymmetry is the core of the report.

There is no user-visible impact that I can find: traces are ingested, sign-in works, queues are processed. The concern is that a real Redis fault would be indistinguishable from this noise.

Everything checks out when tested by hand **from inside the web pod**, using the container's own environment variables and CA file:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| DNS for the Sentinel service | resolves to all Sentinel nodes |
| TCP to each Sentinel on 26379 | connects |
| TLS handshake with `REDIS_TLS_CA_PATH` | succeeds, `authorized=true`, SAN covers the name used |
| `AUTH <REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD>` then `SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name` | `+OK`, returns the correct master |
| ioredis client built from `process.env` exactly as `createRedisSentinelInstance` does | **PONG** |

So the configuration the web container is running with is sufficient to connect — yet something inside it does not.

**What the failure signature indicates.** Reproducing the two variants in the pod isolates it to TLS trust on the *Sentinel* connection specifically:

| ioredis options | Result |
|-

title: feat(public-api): add DELETE /api/public/score-configs/{configId}
body:
## Problem

The public REST API for score configurations has GET (list + by id), POST (create), and PATCH (update) on `/api/public/score-configs/{configId}`, but no DELETE. The corresponding MCP tool (`mcp.score_configs.delete`) is already wired to soft-archive a config via the public API's PATCH path, so a user invoking the public API directly has no symmetric way to remove a config.

Today a user wanting to remove a score config has to use the Langfuse UI, which breaks scripted/automated workflows. Public-API consumers (SDK scripts, the existing MCP server, the public Langfuse CLI once it grows score-config commands) need a single, well-defined verb.

## Motivation

A small, real, useful addition. Mirrors the pattern that already exists for `/api/public/traces/{traceId}` and `/api/public/scores/{scoreId}` — both of which expose a DELETE verb on the single-resource route. The score-configs surface is the only major config resource on the public API that doesn't.

The internal soft-archive model (the `isArchived` boolean on the `ScoreConfig` model, written via `prisma.scoreConfig.update` when the MCP tool archives a config) is the existing semantic for "remove a score config from the user's active list." A `DELETE` verb that performs the same soft archive is a 1-to-1 mapping with REST conventions and avoids introducing a new "hard delete" semantic that the rest of the model does not support.

## Background

- Score configs are project-scoped resources exposed by the public API: `web/src/pages/api/public/score-configs/`.
- The current service layer (`web/src/features/public-api/server/score-configs-api-service.ts`) exposes `createScoreConfig`, `updateScoreConfig`, and the re-exported `getScoreConfig` / `listScoreConfigs` — but no archive/delete helper.
- The MCP server's `deleteScoreConfig` tool (`web/src/features/mcp/features/scores/tools/deleteScoreConfig.ts`) is the de-facto "delete" path today: it calls `updateScoreConfig({ body: { isArchived: true } })`. A direc

title: bug: LLM-as-a-judge (EVAL) scores never appear in the Sessions table Scores column — eval worker writes scores with session_id NULL
body:
## Describe the bug

Scores written by the LLM-as-a-judge eval worker (`source = EVAL`) never appear in the **Sessions table's Scores column**, even though every judged trace belongs to a session. The session detail page and the Traces table show the same scores fine — only the Sessions list aggregation is blind to them.

Root cause (verified in ClickHouse and in source, both on our deployed version and on current `main`):

1. **The eval worker writes scores without a session id.** `buildEvalScoreWritePayloads` (`worker/src/features/evaluation/evalScoreEvent.ts`) sets `traceId`, `observationId`, `environment`, … but no `sessionId`, so eval score rows land in ClickHouse with `session_id = NULL` — even when the scored trace has `session_id` set.

2. **The Sessions table aggregates scores by the score's own `session_id`.** Both the current events-based path (`eventsSessionScoresAggregation`, `packages/shared/src/server/queries/clickhouse-sql/query-fragments.ts` — `GROUP BY project_id, session_id` then `ON … sc.score_session_id = s.session_id`) and the older `scores_agg` CTE in `sessions-ui-table-service.ts` join on `scores.session_id`. `NULL` never joins, so EVAL scores are structurally invisible there.

```sql

title: Kiro integration docs target the pre-1.x hook schema; plus three Kiro 1.x findings (usage timing, credits-not-tokens, cost inference double-count)
body:
## Summary

The [Kiro integration page](https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/kiro) and the
[`applications/kiro-langfuse`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-examples/tree/main/applications/kiro-langfuse)
example were written against Kiro's pre-1.x hook system (added via #12677, March 2026).
Kiro IDE 1.x ships a different hook file format and different trigger names, so the
documented hook definitions no longer match what the IDE reads.

While building a Kiro 1.x integration I also hit three behaviours that affect *any*
Kiro→Langfuse integration, not just mine. Writing them down here since they are not
obvious and cost me a while to establish.

## 1. The hook schema changed

Documented today (`.kiro/hooks/langfuse-agent-stop.kiro.hook`):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "Langfuse - Agent Stop",
  "when": { "type": "agentStop" },
  "then": {
    "type": "runCommand",
    "command": "KIRO_HOOK_EVENT=agent_stop node hooks/hook-handler.js"
  }
}
```

What Kiro 1.x reads (`.kiro/hooks/<id>.json`) — this one is running in my workspace
right now:

```json
{
  "version": "v1",
  "hooks": [
    {
      "name": "Langfuse session export",
      "trigger": "Stop",
      "action": { "type": "command", "command": "npx -y kiro-langfuse-export" }
    }
  ]
}
```

Differences: a `hooks` array instead of one hook per file, `version: "v1"`,
`trigger` instead of `when.type`, `action` instead of `then`, `command` instead of
`runCommand`, and PascalCase trigger names (`Stop`, `PostToolUse`,
`UserPromptSubmit`, `PostFileSave`, `PreTaskExec`, …) instead of camelCase
(`agentStop`, `postToolUse`, …). Matchers also moved: `PostToolUse` filters on a
regex `matcher` against the tool name rather than a `toolTypes` array.

I have **not** tested whether Kiro 1.x still accepts the legacy `*.kiro.hook`
format as a fallback, so I can't say the current docs are outright broken — only
that they describe a different schema than the one 1.x documents and uses. Worth
confi

title: bug(sdk-js): LangGraph control-flow exceptions are reported as errors
body:
### Describe the bug

When `@langfuse/langchain` is used as a LangChain callback for a LangGraph workflow, LangGraph control-flow exceptions are exported as `ERROR` observations.

LangGraph uses `GraphBubbleUp` descendants such as `GraphInterrupt` and `ParentCommand` to pause or route graph execution. These values have `is_bubble_up === true` and are not application failures. However, `CallbackHandler` currently assigns `level: "ERROR"` unconditionally in `handleChainError`, `handleRetrieverError`, `handleToolError`, and `handleLLMError`.

Expected behavior: LangGraph control-flow exceptions should retain their status message but use the default observation level. Ordinary errors should continue to use `ERROR`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a LangGraph `StateGraph` with a node that calls `interrupt(...)`.
2. Compile it with a checkpointer such as `MemorySaver`.
3. Invoke it with `new CallbackHandler()` in the callbacks list.
4. Inspect the exported Langfuse observations.

The observation whose status message contains `GraphInterrupt` is currently marked as `ERROR`, even though the graph paused normally for human input.

The same misclassification occurs for a child graph that returns:

```ts
new Command({
  graph: Command.PARENT,
  goto: "after",
  update: { route: "from-child" },
});
```

The graph routes successfully, but the `ParentCommand` observation is marked as `ERROR`.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Langfuse Cloud. The classification happens in the JavaScript SDK before export, so self-hosted deployments are affected as well.

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

Not applicable.

### SDK and integration versions

* `@langfuse/langchain`: 5.9.1
* `@langchain/core`: 1.2.3
* `@langchain/langgraph`: 1.1.4

### Additional information

The proposed fix checks the LangGraph control-flow marker structurally (`is_bubble_up === true`) so that `@langchain/langgraph` does not need to become a runtime dependency of `@langfuse/langchain`. Regressi

## feat(public-api): add DELETE /api/public/annotation-queues/{queueId}

### Problem

The Langfuse public API exposes `GET`, `POST` on `/api/public/annotation-queues`, `GET` on `/api/public/annotation-queues/{queueId}`, and full CRUD on `/api/public/annotation-queues/{queueId}/items` and `/api/public/annotation-queues/{queueId}/assignments`. There is, however, no public-API way to **delete an annotation queue itself**. A user (or programmatic SDK caller) can create, list, and inspect queues, but to remove a queue they have to fall back to the UI or the tRPC `annotationQueue.delete` mutation.

This is a parity gap with the rest of the public API. `DELETE` already exists for:

- `/api/public/traces/{traceId}` (`#11xxx` family)
- `/api/public/scores/{scoreId}` (`#11467`)
- `/api/public/comments/{commentId}` (`#15444`)

`DELETE /api/public/annotation-queues/{queueId}` deletes the queue and (via existing Prisma `onDelete: Cascade` on `AnnotationQueueItem` and `AnnotationQueueAssignment`) all of its items and assignments. The companion `GET /api/public/traces` and `GET /api/public/sessions` endpoints both already support `fromTimestamp` / `toTimestamp` (ISO-8601, see `web/src/features/public-api/types/traces.ts` and `web/src/features/public-api/types/sessions.ts`); comments is the odd one out.

### Use case

A team is reviewing 8k comments generated during a 30-day window of a launch. Today the only way to bound the result set is client-side — fetch everything, drop what doesn't fall in `[fromTimestamp, toTimestamp)`. For a long project, that's a multi-MB response and 30+ round trips, all to recover what should be a 1-line filter on the server.

### Current behavior

`GET /api/public/comments?page=1&limit=50&objectType=TRACE` returns the first 50 comments across the project's entire history, ordered by some default. Adding `fromTimestamp=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z&toTimestamp=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z` has no effect — both params are silently ignored (the route's `querySchema` is `GetCommentsV1Query`, which does not declare them, so they're stripped during `parse`, and the service has no `createdAt` filter).

Either bound is optional. A request with `fromTimestamp` only returns comments on or after that time; a request with `toTimestamp` only returns comments strictly before that time (matches the existing `traces` and `sessions` semantics). Invalid timestamps return 400 (the existing Zod schema for `stringDateTime` already throws on malforme

The "root total cost / duration" values used for heatmap colour scaling in the trace detail view are computed in **four separate places, with four different formulas**. The same trace therefore gets different heatmap colours depending on which view renders it.

Two existing `TODO` comments already ask for this logic to be extracted to a shared utility, but they describe it as duplication only — as far as I can tell the fact that the copies *disagree* isn't recorded anywhere.

| # | Location | Duration formula |

## Summary

In-app agent runs are rate limited at **organisation scope only**. There is no per-user cap, so a single user can consume the entire organisation's agent quota and lock out everyone else in the org. Two `TODO`s in the code state this explicitly.

Raising it because the feature bills real LLM spend, which makes the noisy-neighbour case more than a fairness question.

Observed on `main` @ `ae84d6a39` (v4.3.1).

## Affected code

`web/src/features/in-app-agent/server/rateLimit.ts:16-22`

```js
/**
 * Build the org-scoped rate-limit scope for an in-app agent request.
 *
 * Shared by the foreground route and the background `startRun` mutation so a
 * user cannot bypass the cap by submitting through the other path.
 *
 * TODO: this is org-scoped only; there is no per-user cap yet.
 */
export function getInAppAgentApiAccessScope(...)
```

`web/src/features/in-app-agent/server/handler.ts:240`

```js
// TODO: Add an additional user-level cap once the rate-limit service supports non-org keys.
const rateLimitResponse = await rateLimitInAppAgentRequest(
  rateLimitScope,
  "in-app-agent-run",
);
```

The returned scope carries a fixed `apiKeyId: "in-app-agent-session"` / `publicKey: "in-app-agent-session"` for the admin path, i.e. every session shares one identity from the rate limiter's point of view.

The blocker is named in the second TODO: `RateLimitService` currently keys on org-derived identifiers and has no non-org key support.

- **Quota exhaustion by one user.** Any single member — scripted loop, runaway retry, or just heavy interactive use — can spend the org's entire allowance. Other members get rate-limited with no indication of why.
- **Cost, not just availability.** Agent runs invoke models through the Bedrock/Mastra runtime, so this is a path to material spend on a paid feature.

On a self-hosted v4 deployment brought up with the official `docker-compose.yml`, typing anything into
the Tracing page search box fails. The UI shows an `Internal Server Error` toast with `Path: events.all`
and the table renders empty.

`langfuse-web` logs the underlying ClickHouse error:

```
ClickHouse query failed with non-retryable error: Enable the setting 'enable_full_text_index'
to use function hasAllTokens: In scope SELECT e.span_id AS id, ... FROM events_full AS e
WHERE (e.project_id = '...') AND ...

title: Local dev setup is not covered by any agent skill, and CONTRIBUTING's ClickHouse install path is broken
body:
### Summary

Two related findings from bootstrapping this repo from scratch on macOS. The second is a plain bug in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and is worth fixing independently of the first.

### 1. `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s ClickHouse install path no longer works

`CONTRIBUTING.md` (Development Setup, step 1) says to install the ClickHouse binary via `curl https://clickhouse.com/ | sh`. Following the Homebrew equivalent, `brew install --cask clickhouse`, currently:

- installs a deprecated cask that **removes itself immediately after installing**, and
- leaves an **815 MB** binary behind, which then needs `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` to run.

I hit this by letting an agent set the repo up using only `CONTRIBUTING.md` as its source. It lost roughly ten minutes recovering, ending with a hand-rolled copy out of the Homebrew cache.

The repo already contains a better answer that is not documented anywhere a contributor would look. `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` shims the client through the dev container:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exec docker exec -i langfuse-clickhouse clickhouse "$@"
```

That is 76 bytes instead of 815 MB, and it is the path CI already trusts. Inside the container, the `--host localhost --port 9000` that `clickhouse/scripts/dev-tables.sh` passes resolves to the server itself, so the scripts work unchanged.

Happy to send a small PR that documents the shim in `CONTRIBUTING.md` on its own.

### 2. No agent skill covers local setup

`.agents/skills/` has 31 skills. `infra:dev:up`, `dx` and `corepack` appear in **none** of them. `golang-migrate` and `.env.dev.example` appear only as passing mentions inside `backend-dev-guidelines` and `clickhouse-best-practices` reference docs, never as a procedure.

`seed-test-data` is the closest, and its `pnpm run seed -- doctor` is excellent — but it structurally cannot run before `pnpm install` and `.env` exist, so the bootstrap layer underneath it is uncovered.

Signing in with email/password fails when the email contains leading or trailing whitespace (e.g. from copy-paste, or a mobile keyboard adding a trailing space).
