title: bug: LangChain v1 standard content blocks show as raw JSON in the Formatted trace view
body:
### Describe the bug

The normalized I/O parser (the default for the single-trace Formatted view since #17729) does not recognise LangChain's v1 standard content blocks. `langfuse.langchain.CallbackHandler` records `message.content` as it is (`{"role": ..., "content": message.content}`), so these blocks reach the parser unchanged:

- `image`, `file`, `audio` and `video` blocks (`url`, `base64` or `file_id`, plus `mime_type`), the format the LangChain docs use for multimodal input, become `custom` parts. Images show up as JSON instead of being rendered.
- A `file` block with a `url` is picked up by the AI SDK `file` handler, which reads `mediaType`, so its `mime_type` is dropped.
- `reasoning` blocks (`{"type": "reasoning", "reasoning": "..."}`) produce a reasoning part without text, and the trace view shows `null`.
- `server_tool_call` and `server_tool_result` blocks (server-side tools such as web search) become `custom` parts, so the call is not shown as a tool call and its result is not attached to it.
- `invalid_tool_call` content blocks become `custom` parts next to the flagged call built from `invalid_tool_calls`.

The output-side blocks appear when a chat model stores standard content (`output_version="v1"` or `LC_OUTPUT_VERSION=v1`).

Expected: media blocks become `file` parts with the declared `mime_type` (or a modality wildcard such as `image/*`), reasoning blocks carry their text, `server_tool_call` / `server_tool_result` become a provider-executed tool call and its paired result, and an `invalid_tool_call` block becomes the same flagged call as its `invalid_tool_calls` entry.

### Steps to reproduce

Block shapes are from the LangChain docs ([multimodal](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal), [standard content blocks](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#standard-content-blocks)) and `langchain_core/messages/content.py`. title: bug: dashboard cost widgets round sub-cent totals to $0.00
body:
### Describe the bug

Since #15866, `costFormatter` (`web/src/utils/numbers.ts`) always rounds to two decimals.
Any dashboard cost total below half a cent is therefore shown as `$0.00`.

With cheap models this is the normal case, not an edge case. Our project runs
`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` at about $0.0006 per call. On the Home dashboard the
"Model costs" card shows **Total cost $0.00**, and every model row shows $0.00.
The trace detail for the same call correctly shows **$0.000601**.

The stored data is correct: `total_cost` in ClickHouse is 0.000601. Only the display
rounds it away.

**Expected:** a non-zero cost is never shown as `$0.00`. Totals of one cent or more keep
the cent precision that #15866 introduced.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Self-hosted v4.54.0. `main` as of 2026-10-08 has the same `costFormatter`.
2. Ingest one generation with `cost_details={"total": 0.000601}`, or use token usage on
   any model priced at a fraction of a cent per call.
3. Open the Home dashboard. "Model costs" shows `$0.00`, for the total and the per-model row.
   The totals of "Model Usage" and "User consumption" are formatted the same way.
4. Open the trace: the generation shows `$0.000601`.

Affected call sites (all use `costFormatter`): `ModelCostTable.tsx` (total and per-model
USD), `ModelUsageChart.tsx` (`totalMetric`), `UserChart.tsx` (`totalMetric`).

### Proposed fix

Keep two decimals from $0.01 up. Below one cent, keep about three significant digits:

```ts
export const costFormatter = (totalCost?: number) => {
  const cost = totalCost ?? 0;
  // Sub-cent costs (cheap models) would round to $0.00; keep ~3 significant digits.
  if (cost !== 0 && Math.abs(cost) < 0.01) {
    const digits = 2 + Math.ceil(-Math.log10(Math.abs(cost)));
    return usdFormatter(cost, 2, Math.min(digits, 10));
  }
  return usdFormatter(cost, 2, 2);
};
```

Every value in the #15866 test stays the same: `$4.40`, `$0.07`, `$0.02`, `$0.00`.
New cases: `0.000601 → $0.000601`, `0.004 → $0.004`, `0.00

title: bug: OpenInference llm.token_count.prompt_details.audio is not subtracted from input tokens
body:
### Describe the bug

OTel spans from OpenInference instrumentations (openai, litellm, llama_index) carry `llm.token_count.prompt_details.audio`, which is a subset of `llm.token_count.prompt`. The generic OTel usage mapping in `OtelIngestionProcessor` subtracts `prompt_details.cache_read` / `cache_write` from `input`, and since #15415 it also handles `completion_details.audio`, but `prompt_details.audio` is skipped.

Result: `input` still includes the audio tokens, they get priced at the text input rate instead of `input_audio_tokens`, and a raw `prompt_details.audio` key shows up in usage details. OpenAI reports `audio_tokens: 0` on most normal chat calls, so nearly every OpenInference OpenAI generation gets a stray `prompt_details.audio: 0` entry.

Expected: `input` = prompt minus audio, with the audio count stored as `input_audio_tokens`, the same way `completion_details.audio` becomes `output_audio_tokens`.

### Steps to reproduce

Ingest an OTel span with:

- `llm.token_count.prompt` = 1000
- `llm.token_count.prompt_details.audio` = 200
- `llm.token_count.completion` = 50
- `llm.token_count.total` = 1050

Usage details come out as `input: 1000, "prompt_details.audio": 200`. Expected `input: 800, input_audio_tokens: 200`.

#15415 called this attribute out as out of scope.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Self-hosted

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

main @ eecc7d0

### SDK and integration versions

openinference-instrumentation-openai (current PyPI)

### Are you interested in contributing a fix for this bug?

Yes, PR coming shortly.

title: bug: recurring Worker Redis socket timeouts; upstream ioredis reconnect fix not included
body:
### Describe the bug

The self-hosted Langfuse Worker repeatedly logs `Socket timeout. Expecting data, but didn't receive any in 30000ms` after a period of heavy OTLP ingestion. Some queues subsequently repeat the error approximately every 31.5 seconds while the Worker remains Ready and Redis continues to answer commands.

There is an upstream ioredis reconnect defect that appears relevant: [redis/ioredis#2147](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/issues/2147), fixed by [redis/ioredis#2148](https://github.com/redis/ioredis/pull/2148). A timer belonging to a closed stream can survive reconnection and destroy a replacement stream, even after that stream has returned data. The fix clears the timer on close and binds its callback/listener to the owning stream.

Our Worker runs ioredis 5.10.1. A source review of the latest Langfuse v4.56.0 also found ioredis 5.10.1 in the lockfile, with no ioredis patch. This report asks to track inclusion of the upstream fix; **we have not established that this defect caused every timeout in our deployment, nor identified the initial trigger for the first synchronized timeout burst.**

Expected behavior: retain socket timeout protection, but prevent timers from a previous connection from terminating a recovered connection.

### Steps to reproduce

The following is an observed production sequence, not an isolated deterministic Langfuse reproduction:

1. Run the self-hosted Worker with `REDIS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS=30000` and the environment described below.
2. Process a burst of OTLP ingestion, including spans that trigger the oversized-span warning.
3. Observe socket timeout errors tagged with at least 27 queue names nearly simultaneously.
4. After the burst, some clients continue logging the same timeout at roughly 31.5-second intervals, although Redis is responsive and periodic jobs continue progressing.

title: feat(evals): support multiple named scores and per-dimension reasoning in a single LLM-as-a-Judge call
body:
### Feature request

Allow a standard LLM-as-a-Judge evaluator to define multiple named outputs and produce all scores, with per-dimension reasoning, in a single model call.

### Use case

We evaluate agents’ tool-use quality across several related dimensions:

- **Argument accuracy:** Were the correct tools called with appropriate arguments?
- **Workflow correctness:** Were tool calls ordered correctly, including dependencies and error handling?
- **Result utilization:** Did the agent correctly use tool results in its subsequent actions and final response?

All three dimensions need the same conversation and tool-call history, typically 5K–20K characters.

Currently, we need three separate LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators attached to the same evaluation rule. This sends essentially the same context in three separate model calls, increasing input-token costs and potentially latency. Independent evaluation also makes it harder to assess these related dimensions coherently.

### Current behavior and related work

Based on the v4.56.0 implementation, standard LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators still have a single output definition. NUMERIC and BOOLEAN outputs produce one score.

We found these related capabilities:

- [#12540](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/12540): categorical multi-match outputs can produce multiple score records, but they share the same score name and reasoning.
- [#17733](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/17733) and [#18389](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/18389): decision-model evaluators support multiple named scores in one call. However, we want to keep using our existing general-purpose judge models and receive textual reasoning for each dimension.
- [#13685](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/13685): code evaluators support multiple scores, but their network restrictions prevent calling an external judge model directly.

An external custom evaluator can work around this by calling the judge once and writing multiple scores t

title: fix(tracing): an expanded system prompt can only be collapsed from the bottom of the prompt
body:
## What

Long system prompts collapse to a 4-line preview by default. Once expanded, the **only** way back is a `Collapse system prompt` link rendered *after* the entire prompt body — so on a multi-thousand-token prompt you have to scroll through the whole thing to hide it, which defeats the point of collapsing.

It is worse than a one-off annoyance, because the expanded/collapsed choice is a **persisted, global preference** (`localStorage.collapseSystemPrompt`, `web/src/hooks/useCollapsibleSystemPrompt.ts`). Expand once and every system message on every trace afterwards renders expanded, each with its exit at the bottom.

`web/src/components/ui/MarkdownViewer.tsx` — a single control, built at L550 and rendered at L598 (plain-string path) and L619 (content-parts path), in both cases *after* the content:

title: Flaky test: batchExport scores export asserts an order the query does not define
body:
`worker/src/__tests__/batchExport.test.ts` → `should export scores with filter and sorting` fails intermittently in CI with:

```
AssertionError: expected 'relevance' to be 'accuracy'
❯ src/__tests__/batchExport.test.ts:1093:26
```

The fixture gives two of its scores (`accuracy` 0.85 and `relevance` 0.75) the **same** `timestamp` (`2024-01-01`), exports them with `orderBy: { column: "timestamp", order: "ASC" }`, and then asserts which of the two is `rows[0]`. Sorting by `timestamp` alone does not define the order of rows that share a timestamp, so that assertion is a coin flip. It normally lands green only because the `scores` table is physically ordered by `(project_id, toDate(timestamp), name, id)` and `"accuracy"` sorts before `"relevance"` — rename the fixture score and the test would fail every run.

A few things worth knowing before picking this up:

- **This is a test defect, not an export bug.** The paging layer is deliberately tie-order agnostic — see the `TimestampKeyset` doc comment in `worker/src/features/database-read-stream/getDatabaseReadStream.ts` ("no row is skipped or repeated, whatever order the database returns timestamp ties in"). No row is dropped or duplicated in a real export.
- **The correct pattern is already in this file**, added alongside the keyset paging work: `createScoresWithTiedTimestamps` and `expectEveryScoreOnceInOrder` near the top compare the id *set* and assert only that timestamps are monotonic.
- The assertion dates back to #5949 (March 2025) and is untouched by the recent paging changes — it has been latent the whole time, not a regression.
- A scan of every `it()` block in `worker/src` and `packages/shared/src` found **this one test only**, so no wider cleanup is implied.

title: fix(ui): organization plan badge looks different on the organizations overview page than in the breadcrumb
body:
The organization's plan name is rendered as a badge in two places and the two don't match. The breadcrumb (`web/src/components/layouts/breadcrumb.tsx`) uses the design-system `Badge`. The organizations overview page passes the same string to `Header`'s `label` prop (`web/src/features/organizations/components/ProjectOverview.tsx` → `web/src/components/layouts/header.tsx`), which renders it with `components/ui/StatusBadge` — a status component. A plan name matches none of `StatusBadge`'s status categories, so it falls into the `unknown` branch and comes out as a larger gray pill with a status dot in front of it. A plan is not a status, and the dot reads as liveness. It stayed invisible because `StatusBadge` types its prop as `Status | (string & {})`: passing a non-status is not a type error, and no lint rule covers it.

This is not a one-off. On `main` there are four badge implementations in `web/src`, and the organizations overview page alone uses three of them — the legacy badge for the org's informational label, `StatusBadge` for the plan, and a hand-rolled pill next to each project name.

* legacy `components/ui/badge` — 72 files

title: bug: UBI 9 base in 4.55.0+ ships pcre2 10.40-6.el9 with no available RHEL 9 fix (CVE-2026-86145)
body:
### Describe the bug

The base image change in 4.55.0 (`node:24-alpine` → `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi:9.8`)
introduced `pcre2-10.40-6.el9` into the runtime image. That version is affected by
[CVE-2026-86145](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-86145) — an out-of-bounds
write in `pcre2_dfa_match`, fixed upstream in PCRE2 10.48.

Red Hat has not shipped a fix for RHEL 9. Their Security Data API reports `pcre2` as
`"fix_state": "Affected"` with no errata, and the same for RHEL 8 and 10. The only patched
build anywhere is `pcre2-main-10.48-0.1.hum1` in Red Hat Hardened Images (RHSA-2026:67534),
which this image does not consume.

The effect for self-hosters is that container scanners flag every 4.55.0+ image with an
unactionable Critical/High finding. Moving to a newer 4.x tag does not clear it, because
`dnf upgrade` on `ubi9:9.8` resolves the same package version — verified against a freshly
rebuilt `:4`.

4.54.0 and earlier are unaffected: the alpine-based image does not install pcre2 at all.

### Steps to reproduce


The runtime image intentionally carries no package manager, so the rpmdb has to be queried
externally:

```bash
# 4.56.0 (UBI 9.8) — vulnerable package present
mkdir -p /tmp/lfrpm
docker run --rm --user 0 -v /tmp/lfrpm:/out --entrypoint /bin/bash \
  langfuse/langfuse:4.56.0 -c 'cp -rL /var/lib/rpm /out/rpmdb'

docker run --rm -v /tmp/lfrpm/rpmdb:/rpmdb:ro \
  registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi:9.8 \
  bash -c 'rpm --dbpath /rpmdb -qa | grep pcre'
# pcre2-10.40-6.el9
# pcre2-syntax-10.40-6.el9
# pcre-8.44-4.el9
```

```bash
# 4.54.0 (alpine) — package absent
docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh langfuse/langfuse:4.54.0 \
  -c 'cat /etc/os-release | head -2; echo "pcre pkgs: $(apk info | grep -c pcre)"'
# Alpine Linux 3.24.2
# pcre pkgs: 0
```

Confirm the base image difference directly from source:

```bash
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/v4.54.0/web/Dockerfile | head -2
# FROM --platform=... node:24-alpi

title: fix(ui): detail panel header orphans the options button onto its own row at the pane minimum
body:
The observation detail panel's header puts the title on one row, the action buttons on a second, and the trailing `⋮` options button alone on a third. It is not intermittent. The splitter pane's own minimum — `DETAIL_PANEL_MIN_PX = 360` in `TraceLayoutDesktop.tsx` — leaves 328px of content after the header shell's padding, and the action cluster (`Add to` · `Annotate` · `Comment` · `⋮`) measures 344px. It is 16px short of fitting at a width the layout guarantees, so at the pane's floor the kebab always wraps. Narrow viewports pin the pane there; on a wide screen the same state is one splitter drag away.

The sibling header is the tell, and it is why this is worth more than a width tweak:

- `TraceDetailViewHeader` and `ObservationDetailViewHeader` share three byte-identical layout class strings — title row, title, action cluster — copied into both files rather than shared. `DetailViewHeaderShell` extracted the padding and left the layout behind.
- The only structural difference is where `⋮` goes: the trace header keeps it in the title row, the observation header appends it to the wrapping cluster. That, plus a 312px cluster instead of 344px, is the whole reason one of the two survives.
- The action cluster is `flex-wrap` with no overflow behaviour. A collapse-into-a-menu fallback already exists, but it keys off `useIsMobile()` — viewport width — while the element that is actually too narrow is a resizable pane. The header's own layout switch is already a container query (`@md`, 448px) and matches neither 344px nor 328px, so no number in the code describes the width at which this breaks.

Raising the pane minimum past 344px would fix today and not tomorrow: the cluster's width is content, not a constant (`Comment` becomes `Comments` plus a count badge, `Annotate` is conditional). This belongs in one shared detail-header layout with container-aware action overflow, rather than a per-call-site width tweak.

title: fix(web): keyboard shortcut glyphs are misaligned with the text and icons beside them
body:
In the annotation queue item view, the keyboard hints don't sit on the line they share with the text and icons beside them — in the bottom action bar the `?` and `→` glyphs render below the centre of the words they label and spill past the bottom of the strip. It is worst in the score-field legend one row above (`AnnotationForm.tsx`), where the `↑` `↓` `↵` chips and the `1`…`9` chips are **7px apart vertically in the same row of chips**, which renders the digits as superscripts. Measured on current `main` at 1600×1000, light theme.

- **This is the shared primitive, not this screen.** `KeyboardShortcut` (`web/src/components/design-system/KeyboardShortcut/KeyboardShortcut.tsx`) sizes each key label individually: single-character glyphs get bumped one font step up, everything else gets a flat 2px upward nudge that doesn't scale with `size`. A Tailwind v4 `text-*` utility also sets `line-height`, so the bumped glyph's line box overflows the chip's own fixed height. Design-system components take no `className`, so no call site can correct it — **34 of the 35 usages outside the stories file, across 11 files, use the three variants that still do this**. The fourth variant, `keycap`, already centres its glyphs properly: #18274 fixed it there for tooltips and left the inline variants behind. The fix belongs in the primitive's vertical rhythm, not in the annotation queue.
- Separately, in the same bar: the previous and next buttons each draw their arrow twice — a lucide `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` icon immediately followed by a `KeyboardShortcut` whose glyph for that key is the same arrow (`AnnotationQueueItemPage.tsx`).
- Nothing catches this in Storybook today: every `KeyboardShortcut` story renders the chips on their own or next to each other, never beside the text, icon or button label they are supposed to line up with.

title: docs(review): REVIEW.md enforces a comment form the repo does not use
body:
`REVIEW.md:69` tells reviewers that comments must add information beyond the name and stay terse, "using `/** X does Y [for Z] */`". The automated reviewer reads that trailing clause as a requirement on comment *syntax* and raises `Convention` findings against ordinary `//` comments — it did exactly that on #18659, against `web/next.config.mjs:140`, a comment that is terse, non-speculative, says something the surrounding names do not, and is still in `main` unchanged. The form in that sentence is an example of how short a comment should be, not a decision about which comment marker to use, and line 69 is the only place in the repo that states a comment form at all: `.agents/AGENTS.md` states the same rule purely in terms of content.

It is not a one-off:

- **Code written under the rule overwhelmingly disagrees with it.** In the 372 commits merged since the rule landed on 2026-09-30, new code added **1,532 standalone `//` comments against 703 `/**` openers** — so taken literally, about two of every three comments written since then are a `Convention` violation, in code that was reviewed and merged.
- **This is the second bullet in that section caught over-enforcing.** All 35 Team rules bullets arrived in one commit (#18091) with no earlier version, and #18176 repaired the same failure mode on the effects bullet eight days later — it needed +22/−6 lines of explicit "neither hook is a violation by name alone" hedging to undo one over-tight sentence.
- **The section has no category for a preference.** `REVIEW.md` defines `Convention` as a "new violation of an applicable team rule" that needs a fix before merge, while separately instructing the reviewer to "omit preferences" — so anything written into Team rules acquires merge force whether that was intended or not. That is how one subordinate clause did this, and it is why correcting only the wording of line 69 leaves the mechanism in place.

A direction rather than a design: a style preference needs somewhere to live

title: ci: flaky-test tracking excludes the runs where tests actually fail
body:
Across the last 1000 merge-queue runs of `pipeline.yml` (2026-09-09 → 2026-10-13), 116 failed — 11.6%, or 9.4% once a one-day apt-mirror outage is set aside. Every one of those drops a PR out of the queue. Fixing these is not the bottleneck: the three flakes responsible for most of the recent damage were each root-caused and merged within a day or two of somebody noticing. **Noticing is the slow part**, and `.github/workflows/ci-runtime-analyst.md` — the weekly job that already does week-over-week flaky-test tracking — can't do it, for three independent reasons:

- Its population rules say to exclude failed and cancelled runs from every analysis. But its flake source of truth is the `Retried tests (N):` block printed by `scripts/vitest/ci-reporter.ts`, and that reporter has no success guard — on a failed run it still prints the row, tagged `[failed]`. So the exact signature of a flake that has stopped being survivable gets written into every failed run's log and then discarded by policy.
- It never parses the output of the two worst jobs. `tests-storybook` doesn't appear in the file at all, and `e2e-tests` appears only as a duration to chart. Those two were among the failing jobs in **62 of the 116** failed runs (53%).
- It samples about five runs a week, against 85–272 merge-queue runs a week over that window.

Worth saying up front that retries are not the alternative remedy here: `web/vitest.config.mts` sets `retry: 3` on CI and the storybook project inherits it, and every one of the recent flakes failed all four attempts.

The merge queue's own failures are already a precise, mechanically attributable signal — each failed `merge_group` run names the job, and the job's log names the test. That looks like a better thing to drive flake detection from than a small sample of successful `tests-web` / `tests-worker` logs.

title: bug: the evaluator save check doesn't tell the model what to produce, so saves can time out on self-hosted models
body:
### Describe the bug

Before saving an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator, Langfuse calls `testModelCall` (`packages/shared/src/server/llm/testModelCall.ts`). The request sets `response_format: json_schema` and sends this prompt:

> Generate one example response that conforms to the provided JSON schema. Respect the type, allowed values, and bounds of every field. Keep any reasoning brief.

Structured output constrains which tokens the model may produce, but on servers like vLLM the schema isn't shown to the model as text. So the prompt never tells the model what fields to fill in, or what they mean. It even refers to "the provided JSON schema", which the model can't see.

On self-hosted models served with grammar-constrained decoding (vLLM's structured outputs, in our case), this often goes wrong. The model concludes it doesn't know what to produce, and may try to ask for the schema. The grammar forces JSON, so the output starts valid and then degenerates into whitespace at the first value the model won't commit to:

```text
{"reasoning": "I don't see the JSON schema in your message. Please provide it, and I'll generate a valid example."  \n  , "score":     \n  \n  \n\n  \n\n  \n ...
```

The call sets no output-token limit, so this continues until the model's own limit. That exceeds the 95-second preflight timeout, and the save fails, from the UI and from the MCP `createEvaluator` tool alike:

> The model did not respond within 95 seconds during evaluator validation. The evaluator was not saved.

The same LLM connection works in the playground.

**Measurements.** We replayed the preflight request against our models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM), with a boolean `score` and a string `reasoning` schema, the output capped at 2,000 tokens so a runaway shows up as `finish_reason: "length"`, and three runs per model and setting. Models: GLM-5.3 (default reasoning and `reasoning_effort: low`) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (default and `reasoning_effort: none`), 12 runs per pro

title: bug: in-flight prompt reads can repopulate the cache after invalidation
body:
### Describe the bug

An in-flight prompt read can cache an old resolved prompt under the new cache epoch after a prompt mutation has committed and invalidation has completed. Later requests can then receive the old prompt until another invalidation or cache expiry.

Reproduced in a deterministic unit test against commit 5cb0a3d37172d9fdf7a07b48ab4c1951dea553df (package version 4.58.0), using the real PromptService with fake Prisma and Map-backed Redis. The test fails against the original implementation: the second request receives version 1 instead of version 2. I have not reproduced this against a running deployment.

### Steps to reproduce

The unit test controls this interleaving with promises, without sleeps:

1. Start a cache-miss read of a prompt's production label under epoch E1.
2. Let it read version 1 from the database, then pause dependency resolution before the cache fill.
3. Change fake Prisma to return version 2, representing a committed promotion, then call the real invalidateCache method to rotate the project cache epoch to E2.
4. Resume the original read.
5. Fetch the production prompt again.

The original implementation computes a fresh cache key during step 4 and stores version 1 under E2. Expected: the old request may finish with version 1, but subsequent requests must not read that stale fill from the new namespace.

### Code evidence

In [PromptService](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/5cb0a3d37172d9fdf7a07b48ab4c1951dea553df/packages/shared/src/server/services/PromptService/index.ts#L49-L80), getPrompt performs the database read between cache lookup and cache fill. getCachedPrompt and cachePrompt independently call getCacheKey (lines 153 and 168), which reads the current epoch.

The same class's getPromptListCount captures its key before computing the count (lines 205-227), explicitly preventing this ordering hazard. Related history: #12363 and #18348.

title: bug: TOOL observations render their input as a User message and output as an Assistant message
body:
## Describe the bug

The Formatted preview shows a `TOOL` observation's input under a **User** heading and its output under an **Assistant** heading. A bash tool call reads as if the user typed the command and the assistant replied with the command output.

The preview passes every observation's input and output through the ChatML normaliser. When the value is not already a chat message, input gets the fallback role `user` and output gets `assistant` (`packages/shared/src/utils/normalized-io/core/accumulator/collect.ts`, lines 246 and 307 at `df7df89`). The normaliser does not look at the observation type.

## To reproduce

Send an OTel span with OpenInference attributes:

```
openinference.span.kind = TOOL
tool.name               = bash
input.value             = {"command": "ls -R"}
output.value            = .:
```

Langfuse stores it as type `TOOL`, with the input and output above. Open it, and the Preview tab in Formatted mode shows "User: ls -R" and "Assistant: .:".

## Expected behaviour

For a `TOOL` observation, the preview shows the input as the tool call's arguments and the output as the tool result, with labels such as "Tool input" and "Tool output".

## Workaround

The exporter wraps the input as an OpenAI assistant message with one `tool_calls` entry, and the output as a `role: "tool"` message with the same `tool_call_id`. The preview then shows a tool call and its result. The cost is that `input` no longer holds the plain arguments, so filters and evaluators on tool input must read the wrapped form.

## Proposed fix

When the observation type is `TOOL`, and the input and output do not already parse as chat messages, render them as a tool call and a tool result instead of using the user and assistant fallback roles. I can open a PR if this approach suits you.

## Langfuse version

Langfuse Cloud (US), 2026-10-14.

title: fix(ui): row-resize cursor flickers on every row boundary while moving through table rows
body:
### What happens

Moving the pointer vertically through rows in a data table makes the cursor flicker between the row's normal pointer cursor and the `row-resize` cursor. Every row boundary the pointer crosses produces one flicker, so a single sweep down a table produces one per row. It reads as the table twitching under the mouse rather than as an affordance being offered.

Seen on the observations table in the tracing section. The table component is shared, so every table with row resizing enabled behaves the same way.

### Why

Row resizing puts a hit strip on every row's bottom border, in `web/src/components/table/data-table.tsx`:

```ts
/** Each side of the 6px strip centered on the row's bottom border. */
const ROW_RESIZE_HALF_PX = 3;
```

The strip is always live — there is no dwell, no hysteresis, no velocity check — so the cursor swaps the instant the pointer enters it and swaps back on the way out. Row height is user-controlled down to `MIN_CUSTOM_ROW_HEIGHT_PX = 28`, and at that floor roughly a fifth of the table's vertical travel is resize zone. Crossing it is unavoidable when moving between rows, which is the common case; actually wanting to resize is the rare one.

### Suggested fix

Make the pointer earn the resize cursor instead of being handed it:

- show `row-resize` only once the pointer has been inside the strip for a short dwell (~80–150ms) **and** has stayed within a pixel or two for that time
- cancel the pending timer on exit, so a pass-through never changes the cursor at all
- keep `pointerdown` immediate — a deliberate press on the border should still start the drag with no delay, so the affordance is not made slower for the person who actually wants it

Vertical speed is the discriminator that separates the two intents cleanly: someone travelling between rows crosses 6px in a frame or two, someone aiming at the border stops moving.

### Notes

- Pointer behaviour only; the keyboard and touch paths are untouched.
- The `last` edge uses `ROW

bug: OneLogin SSO issuer validation conflicts with sign-in discovery URL
body:
### Describe the bug

For organization-level SSO on Langfuse Cloud with **Provider = OneLogin**, the issuer value that passes save-time validation is not the value the sign-in flow expects, so no single issuer value both saves and signs in.

- **On save**, `validateSsoConfig` fetches `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` and requires the returned `issuer` to match the configured one. For OneLogin this only succeeds with the full OIDC issuer, `https://<tenant>.onelogin.com/oidc/2`.
- **On sign-in**, the stored issuer is passed unchanged to NextAuth v4's OneLogin provider, which builds `wellKnown` as `${issuer}/oidc/2/.well-known/openid-configuration`. With the saved issuer this becomes `https://<tenant>.onelogin.com/oidc/2/oidc/2/.well-known/openid-configuration`, which returns 404, so discovery fails.
- With only the tenant URL (`https://<tenant>.onelogin.com`), sign-in would build the correct discovery URL, but saving is rejected because `https://<tenant>.onelogin.com/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns 400.

**Impact:** an organization we support reported that its users cannot complete SSO sign-in to Langfuse Cloud via OneLogin. Neither the full issuer nor the tenant URL works, so we found no way around this in the SSO settings.

**Expected behavior:** when the issuer OneLogin publishes (`https://<tenant>.onelogin.com/oidc/2`) is configured, save-time validation and sign-in use the same discovery URL, and SSO sign-in can be started.

### Steps to reproduce

Prerequisites: a Langfuse Cloud organization with a verified domain, and a OneLogin OIDC application (client ID / secret) on a OneLogin tenant `https://<tenant>.onelogin.com`.

**Case A: full issuer (save succeeds, sign-in fails)**

1. In the organization's SSO settings, add an SSO configuration for the verified domain with Provider = **OneLogin**.
2. Enter the client ID and client secret, and set the issuer to `https://<tenant>.onelogin.com/oidc/2`.
3. Save. Validation passes and the configuration

title: bug(devcontainer): Codespaces setup hangs on a Corepack prompt, and Rust is missing
body:
### What happened

I created a GitHub Codespace from `main` (8d7a8f77c, 2026-10-14) on a 4-core / 16 GB machine using the repo's `.devcontainer`. Two things blocked `pnpm run dx` from working out of the box:

**1.** `postCreateCommand` **hangs forever.** `cp .env.dev.example .env && pnpm i` stops at:

```
! Corepack is about to download https://registry.npmjs.org/pnpm/-/pnpm-12.8.2.tgz
? Do you want to continue? [Y/n]
```

Nobody can answer the prompt during creation, so `pnpm i` never runs. The likely cause: the Dockerfile runs `corepack prepare pnpm@12.8.2 --activate` at build time as `root`, but the Codespace runs as the `codespace` user, whose Corepack cache is empty, so Corepack downloads pnpm again and asks first.

**2. No Rust toolchain.** `cargo` and `rustup` aren't in the image (`mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/universal:6-noble`), but CONTRIBUTING.md lists Rust as a requirement: `pnpm dev` builds the AI gateway, and the worker build compiles `packages/native`. I had to install rustup by hand before the worker would start.

### Workaround I used

```bash
export COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0 && pnpm install
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
pnpm run dx-f   # then `pnpm run dev` again after the documented first-run failure
```

After that, the full stack came up (web, worker, Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis, MinIO) with the seeded demo project.

### Suggested fix

* `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`: add `"containerEnv": { "COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT": "0" }`, so the postCreate install can't block on a prompt.
* Add Rust to the image, e.g. the `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/rust:1` feature in `devcontainer.json`. The crates' own `rust-toolchain.toml` files would still pick the exact toolchain.

I'm happy to open a small PR with both changes if that sounds right to you.u

body:

title: bug: Experiments started from the UI lose their traces when OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER is a ratio sampler
body:
### Describe the bug

Experiments started from the Langfuse UI appear to run (the dataset run items are created and the LLM is called), but almost none of their traces are stored. This happens whenever `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` / `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` in the worker environment set a ratio sampler, which is a common setup for sampling a service's own APM traces.

Cause: the per-call tracer providers that capture Langfuse's own traces (experiment runs, LLM-as-judge executions) are created without a `sampler`:

- `createAiSdkTelemetryCapture` in `packages/shared/src/server/llm/ai-sdk/telemetry.ts`
- `writeInternalTraceViaOtelIngestion` in `packages/shared/src/server/otel/internalTraceOtelWriter.ts`

In `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` 2.x a `BasicTracerProvider` with no `sampler` reads `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` from the environment. Those variables are the standard way to sample a service's own APM traces, so one setting now controls two unrelated things:

1. how much of the Langfuse process's own telemetry is recorded (intended), and
2. how many Langfuse experiment/eval traces are kept (not intended).

On our self-hosted deployment the platform injects `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.01` into the worker and web pods for APM. The capture providers inherit that 1% ratio. For ~99% of captures the root span is non-recording, nothing is exported, and `flush()` returns at `if (matchingSpans.length === 0) return;`, before the S3 upload and queue publish. There is no log line and no error.

Expected: Langfuse's own product traces should not depend on how the host samples its APM telemetry.

Observed: experiments started from the UI create dataset run items and make the LLM call, but almost none of the traces reach ClickHouse (even a 2-item experiment typically ends up with no traces). The run items exist, but the web logs "Trace with id ... not found for project ..." when the linked traces are requested.

title: fix(ui): navigate on row click in the Users and Sessions tables
body:
The Users and Sessions tables are the only two in the observability section of the project nav where the row itself does nothing — the detail view is reachable only by hitting the ID value in the first cell. Traces, Observations, Events, Topics and Alerts all sit one click away in the same section and all navigate on row click, which is what makes these two read as inconsistent. Both are `DataTable` call sites that pass neither `onRowClick` nor `peekView`: `web/src/features/users/UsersTable.tsx` and `web/src/features/sessions/SessionsTable.tsx`.

- Links and controls inside the row must keep their own behaviour — the Sessions table has a User ID column linking to user detail pages, and row-selection checkboxes. That part is already solved generically by `web/src/components/table/shouldIgnoreRowClickTarget.ts`, which `DataTable` consults before the row handler fires and which every table that already navigates relies on. Per-column event plumbing shouldn't be needed.
- **Not a one-off.** 14 of 30 `DataTable` call sites wire row navigation. Of the 16 that don't, **8 have exactly one detail destination for the row and already render it as a link cell** — Users and Sessions, plus the prompts, datasets, dataset runs, dataset items and both annotation-queue tables. (`ScoresTable` is correctly not among them: all of its links point at other entities, so a row has no unambiguous target.)
- Nothing holds the line, which is why it drifted: row navigation is opt-in with no default, none of the 18 custom ESLint rules covers it, and it is not written down as a convention anywhere. Neither table ever had it — this is not a regression, just a prop nobody passed. Worth considering in that direction: a row's destination belongs to the table definition rather than to a prop each caller has to remember.

body:
Title: bug(sdk-python): @observe drops a free function's first positional input when it has a keyword-only cls parameter

## Describe the bug

A normal free function with a keyword-only parameter named `cls` loses its first positional argument from the input captured by `@observe(capture_input=True)`. The wrapped function still receives that argument and returns the correct value. Both synchronous and asynchronous functions are affected.

For `classify("hello", cls="news")`, the expected captured input is:

```python
{"args": ("hello",), "kwargs": {"cls": "news"}}
```

The actual captured input is:

```python
{"args": (), "kwargs": {"cls": "news"}}
```

## Steps to reproduce

The following reproducer uses the public decorator and an in-process fake client/span. It requires no Langfuse instance or credentials, creates no exporter, and makes no provider calls. Save it as `issue_repro.py` in an environment containing the SDK and its runtime dependencies. Run `python issue_repro.py --assert-contract`. For a clean source checkout plus a separate dependency directory, run `python issue_repro.py /path/to/langfuse-python /path/to/deps --assert-contract`.

```python

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# For a source checkout, supply its root and the installed dependency directory.
if len(sys.argv) >= 3 and not sys.argv[1].startswith('--'):
    sys.path[:0] = [str(Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()), str(Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve())]

from langfuse import observe

implementation = importlib.import_module('langfuse._client.observe')
captured = []

class FakeSpan:
    def __enter__(self): return self
    def __exit__(self, *exc): return False
    def update(self, **kwargs): return self
    def end(self): return self

class FakeClient:
    def start_as_current_observation(self, **kwargs):

        return FakeSpan()

implementation.get_client = lambda **kwargs: FakeClient()

title: fix(ui): group Playground under Evaluation in the project sidebar
body:
In the project sidebar, **Playground** sits in the same navigation group as **Skills** and **Prompts** (`group: RouteGroup.PromptManagement` in `web/src/components/layouts/routes.tsx`). With the `internalFeatures` flag on, that group renders under the heading **Context Management** — which reads as the things that make up a model's context, i.e. prompts and skills. The playground is where you run a prompt against a model and look at what comes back, so it belongs with the evaluation surfaces (Scores, Evaluators, Human Annotation, Datasets, Experiments).

Two things worth knowing before picking this up:

- **The move can't be scoped to the internal heading.** No route declares `RouteGroup.ContextManagement` — 3 routes declare `PromptManagement`, 0 declare `ContextManagement`. The heading is produced by `applyNavigationFilters` in `web/src/components/layouts/app-layout/utils/navigationFilters.ts`, which rewrites the entire `Prompt Management` group when internal features are enabled, so the two headings hold identical items by construction and moving Playground moves it in the default sidebar too. That is a product decision, not a technical one; and if the two groupings are ever meant to differ, the group belongs on the route rather than in a render-time rewrite.
- **The codebase already splits them one field over:** Playground is `productModule: "playground"`, while Skills and Prompts are both `productModule: "prompt-management"`. The sidebar group is the only place the three are treated as one thing.

title: bug: environment badge in the page header is no longer dismissible by clicking it
body:
The cloud environment badge in the page header — `PROD-EU`, `STAGING`, `DEV` — used to be clickable, and one click hid it. That is how clean product screenshots get taken for the docs. Clicking it now does nothing.

- The old dismissal was component state inside `PageHeader`, so the badge came back on the next navigation. Hiding it for the rest of the session is what the screenshot use case actually wants — and the fact that it only survived one page view is probably why nobody noticed it going away.

title: bug: signing out does not invalidate the JWT session token on the server
body:
### Describe the bug

Langfuse uses NextAuth's JWT session strategy. Signing out only clears the session cookie in the browser. The token itself stays valid on the server until it expires (14 days by default). So anyone who copied the token before sign-out, for example from a shared machine, browser extension, proxy log or XSS, can keep using that session after the user has logged out.

Expected: after sign-out, the token from that session is rejected, as already happens after "Sign out of all sessions" and after a password reset.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to Langfuse in a browser.
2. In devtools, copy the `next-auth.session-token` cookie (`__Secure-next-auth.session-token` on HTTPS).
3. Click **Sign out**.
4. Send a request with the copied cookie, e.g.
   `curl -H "Cookie: next-auth.session-token=<copied value>" https://<host>/api/auth/session`
5. The response still contains the signed-in user, and the token still works on authenticated pages and tRPC calls.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Self-hosted

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

v4.53.0 (OSS). Also reproduced on current `main`.

### Additional information

This came up in an enterprise penetration test of our self-hosted Langfuse deployment. Invalidating the session on the server at logout is a requirement for us to pass that review. It maps to OWASP ASVS 4.0 **V3.3.1** ("Verify that logout and expiration invalidate the session token…"), and pentests and security questionnaires for enterprise deployments commonly check for it. Other enterprise self-hosters are likely to hit the same finding.

Langfuse already has a server-side revocation boundary: the session callback rejects tokens issued before the user's sessions-expired-at timestamp, which "Sign out of all sessions" and password reset both advance. Sign-out doesn't advance it. A fix is to do that in NextAuth's `events.signOut` handler. The token carries the user's email, so this costs one database write per sign-out and ad

title: Unauthenticated trace-to-project mapping oracle at /trace/<traceId>
body:
## Summary

`GET /trace/<traceId>` (`web/src/pages/trace/[traceId].tsx`) resolves a trace ID to its owning project with no session check at all. The handler calls `getTracesByIdsForAnyProject([traceId])` and redirects to `/project/<projectId>/traces/<traceId>` on a hit, returns 404 on a miss, and renders a distinct "duplicates found" page when the ID exists in more than one org. No session. No org scoping.

Anyone who can reach the deployment, unauthenticated and across orgs, can therefore enumerate trace IDs and read back which project owns each one. The 302 destination hands over the projectId directly. The 404 confirms an ID does not exist, and the duplicates page reveals that an ID is reused across organizations, which is itself information about org-internal ID collisions. Trace IDs are not secret, since they surface in exported data, logs, and integrations. The mapping from ID to project is the disclosure, and this endpoint is an unauthenticated oracle for exactly that mapping.

## Proposal

Require an authenticated session before the lookup, and scope the query to the organizations that session can actually see before any redirect is produced. If the route's purpose is logged-out redirect convenience, it could instead authenticate first and 404 rather than reveal. The `getTracesByIdsForAnyProject` helper belongs to internal jobs. It should never have backed a public page handler in the first place.

## Reproducer

```bash
# against any deployment, no cookies or API keys:
curl -sI https://<host>/trace/<some-trace-id> | head -1
# 302 → Location: /project/<projectId>/traces/<trace-id>   (owning project leaked)
# 404 → the trace does not exist anywhere
```

Found during an external review of the current tree (`web/src/pages/trace/[traceId].tsx:6`).

title: In-app-agent MCP tool-allowlist upgrade via client-controlled header
CI failure Slack alert fires on cancelled runs, and then has no failure to report
body:
`all-ci-passed` in `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` posts `❌ CI failed on <branch>` for runs that were **cancelled**, not failed. It should only fire when a job actually failed.

The gate deliberately fails itself when any needed job's result is `failure` *or* `cancelled` — that part is right: it is the required branch-protection check and a cancelled run must not go green. The Slack step one step later is gated on bare `failure()`, which is true by then because the gate just failed itself, so a cancellation and a real failure are indistinguishable at the point the alert is sent. The gate's behaviour should stay as it is; the notification should stop inheriting it.

When it misfires the alert has nothing to report: `notify-slack-failure` looks for jobs whose conclusion is `failure`, excluding the gate itself, finds none, and falls back to `Unknown (no failed job found via the Actions API — check the workflow run)`. That string is the signature. At least three runs show it, each with `all-ci-passed` as the only failed job, alongside 14, 1 and 8 cancelled jobs respectively:

- https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/actions/runs/30524794477 (2026-07-30)
- https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/actions/runs/31704624534 (2026-08-13)
- https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/actions/runs/32039842294 (2026-08-18, attempt 3)

The same pattern is duplicated in `notify-docker-image-release` in the same file (`Fail when a release image job failed` → `Notify Slack` on `failure()`), so a fix scoped to `all-ci-passed` leaves half of it in place. `deploy.yml`'s `notify-slack-on-failure` is the shape that already behaves correctly — a separate job with a job-level `if: failure()`, which a cancelled dependency does not trigger.

title: fix(ui): badge text sits 1px off centre in both badge primitives
body:
Badges render their label 1px off centre. Inside the 22px pill the text's line box sits 3.5px from the top and 4.5px from the bottom, so the pill reads as hanging slightly below its own text rather than the text sitting low in the pill. Both badge primitives carry a bottom-only `pb-px` in their base class, and that single pixel is the entire asymmetry — without it the same measurement is 4px / 4px. Both files got it in the same commit, #17609, whose description says the compact pill has "no vertical padding". It is pure box geometry, so it reproduces on every platform and at every device pixel ratio, and it is visible on more than one page header.

- `web/src/components/ui/badge.tsx` — 77 importing files
- `web/src/components/design-system/Badge/Badge.tsx` — 18 importing files

The more useful finding is that this is a house pattern rather than a badge bug: vertical centring is corrected downstream with fixed 1px nudges instead of being owned by the primitive. `DropdownIndicator` exposes a `nudge` prop whose only effect is `translate-y-px` and 49 of its 85 call sites pass it; `translate-y-px` appears at 25 places in `web/src`, one of them in `page-header.tsx`, one level above a chip that is already nudged the other way. The badge is the case where the correction is itself the defect, so the direction worth taking is for the primitives to own their vertical centring rather than adding another call-site correction.

title: feat(otel): support user.name and resourceAttributes fallback in extractUserId (GitHub Copilot OTel compatibility)
body:
### Describe the feature or improvement you'd like

When exporting OpenTelemetry (OTel) traces directly from **GitHub Copilot CLI / VS Code** to Langfuse's `/api/public/otel` endpoint, `sessionId` works out-of-the-box because `OtelIngestionProcessor.extractSessionId` includes `"gen_ai.conversation.id"`.

However, `userId` remains blank in Traces, Users, and Sessions unless an intermediate OTel Collector rewrites attributes, for two reasons in [`packages/shared/src/server/otel/OtelIngestionProcessor.ts`](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/main/packages/shared/src/server/otel/OtelIngestionProcessor.ts):

1. **GitHub Copilot's OTel identity capture emits `user.name`:**
   With [GitHub Copilot's OTel identity capture](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-12-client-telemetry-user-attribution-and-configurable-capture) (`telemetry.capture.identity` / `COPILOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_IDENTITY=true`), Copilot emits:
   - `user.name` (the authenticated GitHub login, following OTel `user.*` semantic conventions) on `invoke_agent` spans
   - `process.user.name` and `host.name` on `resourceAttributes`
   Currently, `extractUserId` only checks `langfuse.user.id`, `user.id`, and metadata compat keys, ignoring `user.name`.

2. **`extractUserId` does not check `resourceAttributes`:**
   When users configure `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES="user.id=..."` or `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES="langfuse.user.id=..."` (which is the standard OTel way to attach static identity/context across all spans in a CLI process), `extractUserId` only inspects `spanAttributes` and ignores `resourceAttributes`—unlike `extractEnvironment`, `version`, and `release` which already fall back to `resourceAttributes`.

### Proposed Solution

Update `extractUserId` in `packages/shared/src/server/otel/OtelIngestionProcessor.ts` to:
1. Check `"user.name"` in addition to `"langfuse.user.id"` and `"user.id"`.
2. Accept `resourceAttributes` as a fallback (checking `langfuse.user.id`, `user.id`, `user.name`, and `process.user.name`

bug: prompt variables with surrounding whitespace are omitted by extractVariables and flagged in editor
body:
### Describe the bug

Prompt variables containing whitespace inside Mustache braces (e.g. `{{ name }}` or `{{ input }}`) are flagged as invalid in the prompt editor and silently omitted by `extractVariables()`.

The runtime compilers (`compileTemplateString` and `compileChatMessages`) explicitly support optional whitespace via `/\{\{\s*([\p{L}\p{N}_.]+)\s*\}\}/gu` and `new RegExp("{{\\s*${varName}\\s*}}", "g")`. However, `extractVariables` in `packages/shared/src/utils/stringChecks.ts` does not trim whitespace from `MUSTACHE_REGEX` captures before running `isValidVariableName`:

```ts
export function extractVariables(mustacheString: string): string[] {
  const matches = Array.from(mustacheString.matchAll(MUSTACHE_REGEX))
    .map((match) => match[1])
    .filter(isValidVariableName);

  return [...new Set(matches)];
}
```

For `{{ name }}`, `match[1]` is `" name "`. `isValidVariableName(" name ")` tests `/^\p{L}[\p{L}\p{N}_]*$/u`, which fails because the leading character is a space.

As a result:
1. `extractVariables("Hello {{ name }}")` returns `[]`.
2. The CodeMirror prompt editor highlights `{{ name }}` with an error diagnostic: `"Variable must start with a letter and can only contain letters, numbers and underscores"`.
3. `renderRichPromptContent` in `PromptReferences.tsx` displays the tag in red (`text-destructive`).
4. New prompts created with padded variables are persisted with `variables: []`.
5. The Playground generates no variable input fields for the prompt.
6. Evaluator variable mapping tables and Prompt Experiment dataset mappings fail to detect the variables.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Langfuse Web, go to **Prompts** -> **New prompt**.
2. Type: `Hello {{ name }}, please summarize {{ text }}.`
3. Click outside the editor:
   - `{{ name }}` and `{{ text }}` are underlined in red with error diagnostics.
   - The "Variables" section below the editor displays no detected variables.
4. Open the prompt in the Playground: no input boxes are rendered for `

title: fix(worker): prevent OTel data loss, early backfill cursor updates, and stuck batch actions
body:
## Problem

There are several worker reliability issues that can cause data loss, incomplete backfills, or batch actions remaining in an incorrect state.

### 1. OTel direct event writes can fail without failing the ingestion job

When `processOtelEvents` writes directly to the events table, `createEventRecord` or `writeEventRecord` can fail after events have already been accepted by `trackTraceBatchActivity`.

The error is currently not propagated to the queue processor in some `shouldWriteToEventsTable` paths.

This can cause the OTel ingestion processor to treat the S3 batch as successfully processed and delete the source batch even though the direct event write failed.

**Expected behavior:** If a direct event write fails, the ingestion job should fail so that the batch can be retried.

### 2. A malformed OTel span can affect processing of valid spans

OTel batch conversion does not consistently distinguish between failures affecting a single span and failures affecting the entire batch.

Problems include:

- A malformed span can cause processing to fail unnecessarily.
- Invalid `traceId` values can cause errors while building the seen-traces set.
- Redis failures in `getSeenTracesSet` can be swallowed and replaced with an empty set.
- Batch-level conversion failures can be returned as an empty result instead of being propagated.

**Expected behavior:**

- Invalid individual spans should be logged and skipped.
- Valid sibling spans should continue to be processed.
- Infrastructure/batch-level failures such as Redis errors should be propagated so the batch can be retried.

### 3. Experiment backfill cursor can advance before ClickHouse persistence completes

`handleExperimentBackfill` currently queues enriched spans and can advance the Redis backfill cursor before the queued records have definitely been flushed to `events_full`.

If the ClickHouse write fails or records remain queued, the cursor may already have moved forward. This can result in records being ski

### Describe the bug

In queries that filter or search via Prisma `contains`, `startsWith`, or `endsWith` with `mode: "insensitive"`, PostgreSQL executes the condition as `ILIKE '%...%'`. When the query string contains `_`, `%`, or `\`, those characters act as SQL wildcards instead of matching literally. A trailing backslash can also trigger a PostgreSQL syntax error.

PR #18873 escaped LIKE wildcards in prompt, dataset list, model, and member searches. However, several active Prisma query builders still execute unescaped substring matches:
1. `stringFilterToPrisma` in `packages/shared/src/server/prismaFilter.ts`: Compiles UI column string filters (`contains`, `does not contain`, `starts with`, `ends with`) for evaluator and evaluation rule tables.

title: Sessions Timeline shows "No messages" when transcript contains an empty thread (nestingLevel 0)
body:
# Sessions Timeline shows "No messages" when transcript contains an empty thread (nestingLevel 0)

**Langfuse version**: 4.63.0
**Feature**: Session Timeline preview (`sessionViewV2Timeline`)

## Problem

Some sessions render "No messages" in the Sessions view even though their traces/observations are complete (trace stats show correct duration/tokens, observation tree has all spans).

## Root cause

The client-side visible-thread filter computes the minimum `currentTurn.nestingLevel` across all threads and only renders threads at that level:

```js
let min = threads.reduce((m, t) => Math.min(m, t.currentTurn.nestingLevel), Infinity)
visibleThreads = threads.filter(t => t.currentTurn.nestingLevel === min)
```

When the transcript contains an **empty thread (0 messages) with `nestingLevel: 0`**, the minimum becomes 0 and the UI renders only that empty thread → "No messages".

## Data (via `events.transcriptByTraceId`, the same tRPC endpoint the UI uses)

| trace | renders | threads |
|---|---|---|
| `3defc925…` | ✅ | 13 threads, all nestingLevel=1, all with messages |
| `b1d52f73…` | ❌ | 3 threads nestingLevel=1 (with messages) + 1 empty thread nestingLevel=0 (0 messages) |
| `1b25f9f8…` | ❌ | 18 threads nestingLevel=1 (with messages) + 1 empty thread nestingLevel=0 (0 messages) |

The empty thread is produced by `assembleTranscript` for spans with empty input/output (failed/empty generation steps).

## Expected

Empty threads should be filtered out or ignored when computing the visible nesting level.

With `LANGFUSE_MIGRATION_V4_WRITE_MODE=dual`, deleting a trace shortly after ingestion leaves its observations in `events_full` and `events_core`. The Python SDK's OpenAI audio-response instrumentation changes the response object returned to the caller. `_extract_chat_response` assigns `audio = kwargs["audio"].__dict__`, then replaces `audio["data"]` with a `LangfuseMedia` object. title: bug: table filters treat `_`, `%` and `\` as LIKE wildcards in Postgres-backed tables
body:
### Describe the bug

`tableColumnsToSqlFilter` in `packages/shared/src/server/filterToPrisma.ts` turns `string` and `stringObject` filters with the `contains`, `does not contain`, `starts with` and `ends with` operators into `ILIKE '%' || $value || '%'` without escaping the value. Postgres reads `_` as any single character, `%` as any sequence and `\` as the escape character, so filters match rows they should not.

#18873, #19024 and #19077 escape these characters in the Prisma filter and search paths. This raw SQL path still binds the value as typed. It backs the prompts table, the `filter` parameter of `GET /api/public/v2/prompts`, the legacy evaluator configs table and the users table filter.

### To reproduce

Call `tableColumnsToSqlFilter` with a `string` filter on the prompts `name` column, operator `starts with` and value `team_a/`. The value is bound unchanged into `ILIKE $value || '%'`, so Postgres also matches a prompt named `teamXa/summary`. The same happens with `does not contain "team_a"`, which then hides `teamXa/summary` too.

### Expected behavior

Only names that start with the literal text `team_a/` match, the same as the other filter and search paths.

### Additional information

Bound value today: `team_a/`. Escaping it with `escapeSqlLikePattern` gives `team\_a/`, which matches literally.

Node.js published a security release on 2026-10-21 fixing 10 CVEs in the 24.x line, including several rated High:
https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases

- CVE-2026-111497 (High): out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder, allowing remote code execution
- CVE-2026-105483 / CVE-2026-106069 (High): TLS certificate hostname verification bypass

title: bug: pi-observability-plugin drops parent spans and mis-nests subagents when subagents run in the same pi process
body:
### Describe the bug

`@langfuse/pi-observability-plugin` assumes one pi session per process. An extension can run subagents as additional `AgentSession`s inside the same pi process, for example with `createAgentSessionRuntime()`. Each of those sessions loads the plugin again. Two things then go wrong.

**1. The parent turn stops exporting after a subagent session is disposed.** `createRuntime()` calls `setLangfuseTracerProvider(provider)`, which writes the single process-wide slot of `@langfuse/tracing` (`globalThis[Symbol.for("langfuse")]`). `startObservation` reads that slot on every call, so once a subagent session has started, the parent's new spans are created on the subagent's provider. When the subagent is disposed, `AgentSessionRuntime.dispose()` emits `session_shutdown` with reason `"quit"` and the plugin shuts that provider down. Every parent span started after that is non-recording and never reaches Langfuse, for the rest of the parent session.

**2. A subagent nests under a sibling subagent instead of the turn that spawned it.** The parent handoff is `process.env` (`LANGFUSE_PI_PARENT_*`), which all sessions in the process share. A subagent started while another subagent's turn is active reads that sibling's turn as its parent.

Expected: the parent keeps exporting for its whole session, and each subagent root is a child of the turn root that spawned it.

### Steps to reproduce

**Library level.** This replays the plugin's call order: the parent and the subagent each create a provider and set the slot, the subagent shuts its provider down, then the parent starts another span.

```js

import { NodeTracerProvider, SimpleSpanProcessor, InMemorySpanExporter } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node";

const mk = () => { const ex = new InMemorySpanExporter(); return { ex, p: new NodeTracerProvider({ spanProcessors: [new SimpleSpanProcessor(ex)] }) }; };
const parent = mk(); setLangfu

title: bug: chat messages on non-GENERATION observations are titled "Input"/"Output" instead of by role
body: ### Describe the bug Since langfuse/langfuse#18787 (4.63.0) the Preview titles messages "Input"/"Output" for every observation type except `GENERATION` (`titleBySide` in `IOPreviewPretty.tsx`). The PR's stated aim is to label *non-chat* I/O (JSON/strings) this way. Here the observation is a `SPAN` whose input/output are real chat messages (`[{"role":"user","content":"…"}]` and `[{"role":"assistant","content":"…"}]`). They are parsed as chat: content is extracted and markdown is rendered. But the headings are "Input"/"Output", never "User"/"Assistant". It is not limited to a single user/assistant pair. With a multi-message conversation as input (e.g. user, assistant, user, assistant, user), **every** message in the input is titled "Input", including the assistant ones, so the preview shows a stack of identical "Input" headings and the roles can't be told apart (the same happens with "Output" on the output side). The role is only recoverable from the message background colour. See the screenshot below. title: bug: images still trust the compromised eMudhra/emSign CA hierarchy, and the usual CA overrides (--use-openssl-ca, SSL_CERT_FILE) cannot remove it
body:
### Summary

Both image variants still trust TLS certificates issued under the eMudhra/emSign hierarchy, including **emSign ECC Root CA - G3** (the hierarchy whose compromised intermediate was removed in the 2026-10-21 Node.js security release, cf. #19177).

For self-hosters this cannot be fixed with the usual CA overrides, because **the OS CA bundle shipped in the images still carries the root**: `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca` and/or `SSL_CERT_FILE` therefore do not remove the trust — they just re-select a store that trusts it. Only replacing the bundle file works.

### To reproduce

On a host that serves a certificate chaining to `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` (test canary `https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/`):

```sh
C='const https=require("https");https.get("https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/",r=>{console.log("TRUSTED",r.statusCode);r.resume()}).on("error",e=>{console.log("rejected",e.code||e.message)})'
docker exec langfuse-langfuse-web-1    node -e "$C"   # -> TRUSTED 200
docker exec langfuse-langfuse-worker-1 node -e "$C"   # -> TRUSTED 200
```

A current host trust store rejects the same chain (`curl` exit 60), so the trust comes from the image, not from the host.

### What the images contain (measured, no mounts)

| image | node | OS CA file | certs | emSign roots present |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `langfuse/langfuse:4` + `langfuse-worker:4` (node:24-alpine base, image v4.52.0) | 24.21.0 | `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, from `ca-certificates-bundle-20260909-r0` | 121 | G1, **G3**, C1, C3 |
| image built from this repo's UBI 9.8 Dockerfile | 24.21.0 | `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt` (`/etc/ssl/certs` is a symlink into `/etc/pki`; **`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` does not exist**) | 146 | G1, **G3**, C1, C3 |

On the alpine variant that file is **fingerprint-identical to Node's compiled-in list** (`tls.rootCertificates`: 121 certificates, identical set), which is why overriding the store cannot help: the "OS store" *is* the st

title: bug: Cmd+K evaluator search disappears after 500ms when typing "evaluator" or "eval"
body:
### Describe the bug

After #18921 added entity search to Cmd+K, `ENTITY_GROUPS.evaluator` defines `keywords: ["evaluator", "eval"]` so typing `"evaluator"`, `"eval"`, or `"eval <name>"` matches evaluators client-side in `toEntityGroup` (same as `"prompt <name>"` or `"queue <name>"`).

However, `useEntityGroups` passes raw `debouncedSearch` directly to `api.evalsV2.options.useQuery({ projectId, limit: ENTITY_LIMIT, search: debouncedSearch.trim() || undefined })`, which filters `name ILIKE '%<search>%'` on the server. When typing `"evaluator"`, `"eval"`, or `"eval answer_relevance"` in Cmd+K, the evaluators show up for the first 500ms (from the initial `search: undefined` query) and then disappear once the debounced query returns `[]` because the evaluator names themselves don't contain `"evaluator"` or `"eval"`.

Also noticed that closing Cmd+K calls `setSearch("")` in `handleNavigate`, `onOpenChange`, and the keydown listener, but never resets `setDebouncedSearch("")`, so reopening Cmd+K keeps the previous `debouncedSearch` until the user types again.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a project with evaluators (e.g. Demo Project with evaluators like `answer_relevance` or `is_cursing`).
2. Press `Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K` and type `evaluator`, `eval`, or `eval answer_relevance`.
3. Matching evaluators appear under the `Evaluators` heading initially, then disappear 500ms later when `debouncedSearch` triggers `evalsV2.options`.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Langfuse Cloud

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

_No response_

### SDK and integration versions

_No response_

### Additional information

Should we strip the `evaluator` / `eval` keywords in `web/src/features/command-k-menu/CommandMenu.tsx` before passing the search term to `api.evalsV2.options.useQuery` (and reset `setDebouncedSearch("")` when the dialog closes), or would you prefer handling multi-term / keyword matching in `listEvaluatorOptions`? Happy to open a PR whichever way you prefer.

title: Cmd+K menu keeps stale debouncedSearch after closing
body: In `web/src/features/command-k-menu/CommandMenu.tsx` (from #18921), closing the Cmd+K menu via `handleNavigate`, `onOpenChange(false)`, or the `Cmd+K` keydown toggle calls `setSearch("")`, but `setDebouncedSearch("")` is not called and `debouncedSearchChange.cancel()` is not run. When you reopen Cmd+K and type a new query, `useEntityGroups` passes the previous session's `debouncedSearch` to `api.evalsV2.options.useQuery` for the first 500ms (and closing within 500ms of typing still fires the pending `debouncedSearchChange`). Is that intentional, or should closing the menu also cancel `debouncedSearchChange` and reset `debouncedSearch` to `""`? Happy to open a quick PR if you want! ss

title: bug: experiment setup failures ignore the selected dataset version
body:
### Describe the bug

When an in-app prompt experiment targets a historical dataset version, a configuration failure causes the worker to create error run items using the latest active dataset items instead of the selected snapshot.

This can associate failures with items added after the selected version and omit items that were active in that snapshot but subsequently archived.

Expected: configuration-error run items should use the same dataset snapshot as normal experiment execution.

### Steps to reproduce

With versioned dataset reads enabled:

1. Create a dataset containing active item A and record dataset version T1.
2. Archive A and add active item B.
3. Start a prompt experiment targeting T1.
4. Make the referenced prompt unavailable before the queued experiment job executes, causing setup validation to fail.
5. Inspect the generated error dataset run items.

Expected: an error run item for A at its historical item version; none for B.

Actual: an error run item for B at its current version; A is omitted.

### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?

Langfuse Cloud

### If self-hosted, what version are you running?

Langfuse v4.70.0, commit f6c3660ce.

### SDK and integration versions

Not SDK-specific; this concerns in-app prompt experiments.

### Additional information

Normal processing passes `config.datasetVersion` to `getDatasetItems`.
`createAllDatasetRunItemsWithConfigError` omits that argument, so selection defaults to latest.

The version must be recovered independently of successful experiment setup: setup can throw before returning its configuration. A valid `dataset_version` should remain usable even when another metadata field is invalid.

Verified through isolated worker execution with mocked external dependencies. Both historical cases produced incorrect item IDs/versions before the fix. The proposed fix passes those cases and preserves latest fallback for missing or malformed versions.

No live deployment or database-backed integration verification

### Describe the bug

A valid prompt export cannot be fully imported into an empty project when a composed prompt appears before its dependency.

Exports are sorted alphabetically by prompt name, while imports create prompts sequentially. If the parent sorts before its child, dependency validation rejects the parent. The child is imported successfully afterward, but the parent is never retried.

This affects project migration and backup/restore workflows involving composed prompts.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a source project, create a text prompt named `z-child` with content `Shared instruction`. Keep it at version 1.

Langfuse Cloud

Langfuse v4.70.0, commit f6c3660ce.

title: bug: OTel generic usage mapping double counts the cache-write TTL breakdown (gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.5m_input_tokens / 1h_input_tokens)
body:
### Describe the bug

A span that carries the cache-write total together with a TTL breakdown has every cache write stored twice:

- `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` (the total)
- `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.5m_input_tokens` and/or `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.1h_input_tokens` (the part of the total written with that TTL)

`extractGenericGenAiUsageDetails` maps the total to `input_cache_creation` and subtracts it from `input`, but it does not know the two breakdown keys. They fall through the passthrough at the end of the function and are stored as extra usage buckets next to the total, so the same tokens now sit in `input_cache_creation` and in `cache_creation.5m_input_tokens`. Everything that sums the usage buckets counts the write twice, and the extra bucket has no price (the Claude default prices define `input_cache_creation_5m` / `input_cache_creation_1h`, not these keys).

The same situation is already handled correctly in the other two Anthropic mappings:

- Vercel AI SDK path, [`OtelIngestionProcessor.ts` L3163-L3200](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/f3500cd1167ec459851730913ebbb94c5003535c/packages/shared/src/server/otel/OtelIngestionProcessor.ts#L3163-L3200): the breakdown is stored as `input_cache_creation_5m` / `input_cache_creation_1h` and subtracted from `input_cache_creation`, then all three are subtracted from `input` ([L3233-L3242](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/f3500cd1167ec459851730913ebbb94c5003535c/packages/shared/src/server/otel/OtelIngestionProcessor.ts#L3233-L3242)).
- REST ingestion, [`ingestion/types.ts` L116-L152](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/f3500cd1167ec459851730913ebbb94c5003535c/packages/shared/src/server/ingestion/types.ts#L116-L152) (`splitAnthropicCacheCreation`): the TTL writes get their own `input_cache_creation_5m` / `_1h` keys and the aggregate keeps only the unattributed remainder, so no write is priced twice.

On custom dashboards, the horizontal bar ("top list") widget shows values like **`8.862K`** and **`3.551K`**. Three decimals after the `K` give you the exact count back, so the label ends up as long as `8,862` but harder to read. The point of compact notation (quick scanning) gets lost.

I'd expect either:

- **`8.9K`**: actually compact, easy to scan (`maximumFractionDigits: 1`), or
- **`8,862`**: the exact count with grouping, which is still short at these sizes.

As far as I can tell, this comes from `formatCompactMetric` in `web/src/features/widgets/chart-library/utils.ts`, which calls `formatFixedMetric(value / divisor, 3, suffix, ...)` with a hardcoded 3 fraction digits. `TopListChart` calls `formatMetric(value, { style: "compact" })` without `maxCharacters`, so nothing trims those digits.

Before #13338 these values went through `compactNumberFormatter` (`Intl.NumberFormat` compact with `maximumFractionDigits: 2`), which gave `8.86K`. body:
## Describe the bug

The Assistant (in-app agent) only sends reasoning provider options for model ids it recognises as Claude (`getInAppAgentReasoningProviderOptions` in `worker/src/features/in-app-agent/runtime/model.ts`). For any other model id it sends none, and there is no setting to add them: `LANGFUSE_AI_EXTRA_HEADERS` only adds headers, not body fields.

So a self-hosted instance that points `LANGFUSE_AI_PROVIDER=anthropic` (or `openai`) at a compatible endpoint serving a non-Claude model runs on whatever the endpoint defaults to. For models that think by default, the thinking tokens take up the per-step output budget (4096 for unknown ids on the Anthropic provider), and runs end with:

> The response hit the model's output limit.

The endpoint accepts `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` and `output_config.effort`, but Langfuse gives operators no way to send them. Today the only workaround is a proxy that rewrites the request body.

Expected: an operator can supply provider options for the Assistant model loop, the same way the built-in defaults are supplied for Claude.

## Steps to reproduce

Self-host Langfuse with `LANGFUSE_IN_APP_AGENT_ENABLED=true`, `LANGFUSE_AI_PROVIDER=anthropic`, `LANGFUSE_AI_BASE_URL` pointing at an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, and `LANGFUSE_AI_MODEL` set to a non-Claude model that thinks by default (we used `glm-5.3-flash` on Zhipu's Anthropic-compatible API).
